description: A distributed version control system for tracking changes in source code and other files.

next.name: am
tip: Apply patches.

option.name: --3way
tip: When the patch does not apply cleanly, fall back on 3-way merge if the patch records the identity of blobs it is supposed to apply to and we have those blobs available locally. --no-3way can be used to override am.threeWay configuration variable.
For more information, see am.threeWay in git-config(1).

option.name: --abort
tip: Restore the original branch and abort the patching operation.
Revert the contents of files involved in the am operation to their pre-am state.

option.name: --allow-empty
tip: After a patch failure on an input e-mail message lacking a patch, create an empty commit with the contents of the e-mail message as its log message.

option.name: --committer-date-is-author-date
tip: By default the command records the date from the e-mail message as the commit author date, and uses the time of commit creation as the committer date.
This allows the user to lie about the committer date by using the same value as the author date.

option.name: --continue
tip: After a patch failure (e.g. attempting to apply conflicting patch), the user has applied it by hand and the index file stores the result of the application.
Make a commit using the authorship and commit log extracted from the e-mail message and the current index file, and continue.

option.name: --directory
tip: These flags are passed to the git-apply(1) program that applies the patch.

option.name: --empty
tip: How to handle an e-mail message lacking a patch:

next.name: drop
tip: The e-mail message will be skipped.

next.name: keep
tip: An empty commit will be created, with the contents of the e-mail message as its log.

next.name: stop
tip: The command will fail, stopping in the middle of the current am session (default).

option.name: --exclude
tip: These flags are passed to the git-apply(1) program that applies the patch.

option.name: --gpg-sign
tip: GPG-sign commits.

The <key-id> is optional and defaults to the committer identity; if specified, it must be stuck to the option without a space. --no-gpg-sign is useful to countermand both commit.gpgSign configuration variable, and earlier --gpg-sign.

option.name: --ignore-date
tip: By default the command records the date from the e-mail message as the commit author date, and uses the time of commit creation as the committer date.
This allows the user to lie about the author date by using the same value as the committer date.

option.name: --ignore-space-change
tip: These flags are passed to the git-apply(1) program that applies the patch.

option.name: --ignore-whitespace
tip: These flags are passed to the git-apply(1) program that applies the patch.

option.name: --include
tip: These flags are passed to the git-apply(1) program that applies the patch.

option.name: --interactive
tip: Run interactively.

option.name: --keep
tip: Pass -k flag to git-mailinfo(1).

option.name: --keep-cr
tip: With --keep-cr, call git-mailsplit(1) with the same option, to prevent it from stripping CR at the end of lines. am.keepcr configuration variable can be used to specify the default behaviour. --no-keep-cr is useful to override am.keepcr.

option.name: --keep-non-patch
tip: Pass -b flag to git-mailinfo(1).

option.name: --message-id
tip: Pass the -m flag to git-mailinfo(1), so that the Message-ID header is added to the commit message.
The am.messageid configuration variable can be used to specify the default behaviour.

option.name: --no-3way
tip: When the patch does not apply cleanly, fall back on 3-way merge if the patch records the identity of blobs it is supposed to apply to and we have those blobs available locally. --no-3way can be used to override am.threeWay configuration variable.
For more information, see am.threeWay in git-config(1).

option.name: --no-committer-date-is-author-date
tip: Disable --committer-date-is-author-date.

option.name: --no-gpg-sign
tip: GPG-sign commits.

The <key-id> is optional and defaults to the committer identity; if specified, it must be stuck to the option without a space. --no-gpg-sign is useful to countermand both commit.gpgSign configuration variable, and earlier --gpg-sign.

option.name: --no-ignore-date
tip: Disable --ignore-date.

option.name: --no-ignore-space-change
tip: Disable --ignore-space-change.

option.name: --no-ignore-whitespace
tip: Disable --ignore-whitespace.

option.name: --no-interactive
tip: Disable --interactive.

option.name: --no-keep
tip: Disable --keep.

option.name: --no-keep-cr
tip: With --keep-cr, call git-mailsplit(1) with the same option, to prevent it from stripping CR at the end of lines. am.keepcr configuration variable can be used to specify the default behaviour. --no-keep-cr is useful to override am.keepcr.

option.name: --no-keep-non-patch
tip: Disable --keep-non-patch.

option.name: --no-message-id
tip: Do not add the Message-ID header to the commit message. --no-message-id is useful to override am.messageid.

option.name: --no-quiet
tip: Disable --quiet.

option.name: --no-reject
tip: Disable --reject.

option.name: --no-rerere-autoupdate
tip: After the rerere mechanism reuses a recorded resolution on the current conflict to update the files in the working tree, allow it to also update the index with the result of resolution. --no-rerere-autoupdate is a good way to double-check what git-rerere(1) did and catch potential mismerges, before committing the result to the index with a separate git-add(1).

option.name: --no-scissors
tip: Ignore scissors lines (see git-mailinfo(1)).

option.name: --no-signoff
tip: Disable --signoff.

option.name: --no-utf8
tip: Pass -n flag to git-mailinfo(1).

option.name: --no-verify
tip: Run the pre-applypatch and applypatch-msg hooks.
This is the default.
Skip these hooks with -n or --no-verify.
See also githooks(5).

option.name: --patch-format
tip: By default the command will try to detect the patch format automatically.
This option allows the user to bypass the automatic detection and specify the patch format that the patch(es) should be interpreted as.
Valid formats are mbox, mboxrd, stgit, stgit-series, and hg.

tip: Mercurial format.

next.name: mbox
tip: mbox format.

tip: mboxrd format.

tip: Stacked Git series format.

option.name: --quiet
tip: Be quiet.
Only print error messages.

option.name: --quit
tip: Abort the patching operation but keep HEAD and the index untouched.

option.name: --quoted-cr
tip: This flag will be passed down to git-mailinfo(1).

option.name: --reject
tip: These flags are passed to the git-apply(1) program that applies the patch.

option.name: --rerere-autoupdate
tip: After the rerere mechanism reuses a recorded resolution on the current conflict to update the files in the working tree, allow it to also update the index with the result of resolution. --no-rerere-autoupdate is a good way to double-check what git-rerere(1) did and catch potential mismerges, before committing the result to the index with a separate git-add(1).

option.name: --resolved
tip: After a patch failure (e.g. attempting to apply conflicting patch), the user has applied it by hand and the index file stores the result of the application.
Make a commit using the authorship and commit log extracted from the e-mail message and the current index file, and continue.

option.name: --resolvemsg
tip: When a patch failure occurs, <msg> will be printed to the screen before exiting.
This overrides the standard message informing you to use --continue or --skip to handle the failure.
This is solely for internal use between git-rebase(1) and git-am(1).

option.name: --retry
tip: Try to apply the last conflicting patch again.
This is generally only useful for passing extra options to the retry attempt (e.g., --3way), since otherwise you'll just see the same failure again.

option.name: --scissors
tip: Remove everything in body before a scissors line (see git-mailinfo(1)).
Can be activated by default using the mailinfo.scissors configuration variable.

option.name: --show-current-patch
tip: Show the message at which git-am(1) has stopped due to conflicts.
If raw is specified, show the raw contents of the e-mail message; if diff, show the diff portion only.
Defaults to raw.

next.name: diff
tip: Show the diff portion only.

next.name: raw
tip: Show the raw contents of the e-mail message.

option.name: --signoff
tip: Add a Signed-off-by trailer to the commit message (see git-interpret-trailers(1)), using the committer identity of yourself.
See the signoff option in git-commit(1) for more information.

option.name: --skip
tip: Skip the current patch.
This is only meaningful when restarting an aborted patch.

option.name: --utf8
tip: Pass -u flag to git-mailinfo(1).

The proposed commit log message taken from the e-mail is re-coded into UTF-8 encoding (configuration variable i18n.commitEncoding can be used to specify the project's preferred encoding if it is not UTF-8).

option.name: --verify
tip: Run the pre-applypatch and applypatch-msg hooks.
This is the default.
Skip these hooks with -n or --no-verify.
See also githooks(5).

option.name: --whitespace
tip: These flags are passed to the git-apply(1) program that applies the patch.

next.name: annotate
tip: Display authorship and last modification commit information for each line in a file, along with the line's content

option.name: --abbrev
tip: Instead of using the default number of hexadecimal digits, use <n> digits, or as many digits as needed to form a unique object name

option.name: --color-by-age
tip: Color line annotations depending on the age of the line in the default format.
The color.blame.highlightRecent config option controls what color is used for each range of age.

option.name: --color-lines
tip: Color line annotations in the default format differently if they come from the same commit as the preceding line.
This makes it easier to distinguish code blocks introduced by different commits.
The color defaults to cyan and can be adjusted using the color.blame.repeatedLines config option.

option.name: --contents
tip: Annotate using the contents from <file>, starting from <rev> if it is specified, and HEAD otherwise.
You may specify - to make the command read from the standard input for the file contents.

option.name: --date
tip: Specify the format used to output dates.
If --date is not provided, the value of the blame.date config variable is used.
If the blame.date config variable is also not set, the iso format is used.
For supported values, see the discussion of the --date option at git-log(1).

option.name: --diff-algorithm
tip: Choose a diff algorithm for moved-line detection.

next.name: histogram
tip: Use histogram diff algorithm.

next.name: minimal
tip: Use minimal diff algorithm.

next.name: myers
tip: Use Myers diff algorithm (default).

next.name: patience
tip: Use patience diff algorithm.

option.name: --encoding
tip: Specify the encoding used to output author names and commit summaries.
Setting it to none makes blame output unconverted data.
For more information see the discussion about encoding in the git-log(1) manual page.

option.name: --first-parent
tip: Follow only the first parent commit upon seeing a merge commit.
This option can be used to determine when a line was introduced to a particular integration branch, rather than when it was introduced to the history overall.

option.name: --ignore-rev
tip: Ignore changes made by the revision when assigning blame, as if the change never happened.
Lines that were changed or added by an ignored commit will be blamed on the previous commit that changed that line or nearby lines.
This option may be specified multiple times to ignore more than one revision.
If the blame.markIgnoredLines config option is set, then lines that were changed by an ignored commit and attributed to another commit will be marked with a ? in the blame output.

option.name: --ignore-revs-file
tip: Ignore revisions listed in <file>, which must be in the same format as an fsck.skipList.
This option may be repeated, and these files will be processed after any files specified with the blame.ignoreRevsFile config option.
An empty file name, "", will clear the list of revs from previously processed files.

option.name: --incremental
tip: Show the result incrementally in a format designed for machine consumption.

option.name: --line-porcelain
tip: Show the porcelain format, but output commit information for each line, not just the first time a commit is referenced.
Implies --porcelain.

option.name: --no-color-by-age
tip: Disable --color-by-age.

option.name: --no-color-lines
tip: Disable --color-lines.

option.name: --no-incremental
tip: Disable --incremental.

option.name: --no-line-porcelain
tip: Disable --line-porcelain.

option.name: --no-porcelain
tip: Disable --porcelain.

option.name: --no-progress
tip: Enable progress reporting on the standard error stream even if not attached to a terminal.
By default, progress status is reported only when it is attached.
You can't use --progress together with --porcelain or --incremental.

option.name: --no-root
tip: Disable --root.

option.name: --no-score-debug
tip: Disable --score-debug.

option.name: --no-show-email
tip: Disable --show-email.

option.name: --no-show-name
tip: Disable --show-name.

option.name: --no-show-number
tip: Disable --show-number.

option.name: --no-show-stats
tip: Disable --show-stats.

option.name: --porcelain
tip: Show in a format designed for machine consumption.

option.name: --progress
tip: Enable progress reporting on the standard error stream even if not attached to a terminal.
By default, progress status is reported only when it is attached.
You can't use --progress together with --porcelain or --incremental.

option.name: --reverse
tip: Walk history forward instead of backward.
Instead of showing the revision in which a line appeared, this shows the last revision in which a line has existed.
This requires a range of revision like <start>..<end> where the path to blame exists in <start>. git blame --reverse <start> is taken as git blame --reverse <start>..HEAD for convenience.

option.name: --root
tip: Do not treat root commits as boundaries.
This can also be controlled via the blame.showRoot config option.

option.name: --score-debug
tip: Include debugging scores for moved-line detection (see -C and -M).

option.name: --show-email
tip: Show the author email instead of the author name

option.name: --show-name
tip: Show the filename in the original commit

option.name: --show-number
tip: Show the line number in the original commit

option.name: --show-stats
tip: Include additional statistics at the end of blame output.

option.name: -b
tip: Show blank SHA-1 for boundary commits.
This can also be controlled via the blame.blankBoundary config option.

option.name: -c
tip: Use the same output mode as git-annotate (blame default off).

option.name: -C
tip: In addition to -M, detect lines moved or copied from other files that were modified in the same commit.
This is useful when you reorganize your program and move code around across files.
When this option is given twice, the command additionally looks for copies from other files in the commit that creates the file.
When this option is given three times, the command additionally looks for copies from other files in any commit.

option.name: -h
tip: Show help message.

option.name: -l
tip: Show long rev (Default: off).

option.name: -L
tip: Annotate only the line range given by <start>,<end>, or by the function name regex <funcname>.
May be specified multiple times.
Overlapping ranges are allowed.

option.name: -M
tip: Detect moved or copied lines within a file.

When a commit moves or copies a block of lines (e.g. the original file has A and then B, and the commit changes it to B and then A), the traditional blame algorithm notices only half of the movement and typically blames the lines that were moved up (i.e. B) to the parent and assigns blame to the lines that were moved down (i.e. A) to the child commit.
With this option, both groups of lines are blamed on the parent by running extra passes of inspection.

option.name: -s
tip: Suppress the author name and timestamp in the output

option.name: -S
tip: Use revisions from <revs-file> instead of calling git-rev-list(1).

option.name: -t
tip: Show raw timestamp (Default: off).

option.name: -w
tip: Ignore whitespace when comparing the parent's version and the child's version

next.name: apply
tip: Apply patches to files and/or the index.

option.name: --3way
tip: Attempt 3-way merge if the patch records the identity of blobs it is supposed to apply to and we have those blobs available locally, possibly leaving the conflict markers in the files in the working tree for the user to resolve.
This option implies the --index option unless the --cached option is used, and is incompatible with the --reject option.
When used with the --cached option, any conflicts are left at higher stages in the cache.

option.name: --allow-binary-replacement
tip: Historically we did not allow binary patch application without an explicit permission from the user, and this flag was the way to do so.
Currently, we always allow binary patch application, so this is a no-op.

option.name: --allow-empty
tip: Don't return an error for patches containing no diff.
This includes empty patches and patches with commit text only.

option.name: --apply
tip: If you use any of the options marked "Turns off apply" above, git apply reads and outputs the requested information without actually applying the patch.
Give this flag after those flags to also apply the patch.

option.name: --binary
tip: Historically we did not allow binary patch application without an explicit permission from the user, and this flag was the way to do so.
Currently, we always allow binary patch application, so this is a no-op.

option.name: --build-fake-ancestor
tip: Newer git diff output has embedded index information for each blob to help identify the original version that the patch applies to.
When this flag is given, and if the original versions of the blobs are available locally, builds a temporary index containing those blobs.

option.name: --cached
tip: Apply the patch to just the index, without touching the working tree.
If --check is in effect, merely check that it would apply cleanly to the index entry.

option.name: --check
tip: Instead of applying the patch, see if the patch is applicable to the current working tree and/or the index file and detects errors.
Turns off "apply".

option.name: --directory
tip: Prepend <root> to all filenames.
If a -p argument was also passed, it is applied before prepending the new root.

option.name: --exclude
tip: Don't apply changes to files matching <path-pattern>.
This can be useful when importing patchsets, where you want to exclude certain files or directories.

option.name: --ignore-space-change
tip: When applying a patch, ignore changes in whitespace in context lines if necessary.
Context lines will preserve their whitespace, and they will not undergo whitespace fixing regardless of the value of the --whitespace option.
New lines will still be fixed, though.

option.name: --ignore-whitespace
tip: When applying a patch, ignore changes in whitespace in context lines if necessary.
Context lines will preserve their whitespace, and they will not undergo whitespace fixing regardless of the value of the --whitespace option.
New lines will still be fixed, though.

option.name: --inaccurate-eof
tip: Under certain circumstances, some versions of diff do not correctly detect a missing new-line at the end of the file.
As a result, patches created by such diff programs do not record incomplete lines correctly.
This option adds support for applying such patches by working around this bug.

option.name: --include
tip: Apply changes to files matching the <path-pattern>.
This can be useful when importing patchsets, where you want to include certain files or directories.

option.name: --index
tip: Apply the patch to both the index and the working tree (or merely check that it would apply cleanly to both if --check is in effect).

Note that --index expects index entries and working tree copies for relevant paths to be identical (their contents and metadata such as file mode must match), and will raise an error if they are not, even if the patch would apply cleanly to both the index and the working tree in isolation.

option.name: --intent-to-add
tip: When applying the patch only to the working tree, mark new files to be added to the index later (see --intent-to-add option in git-add(1)).
This option is ignored if --index or --cached are used, and has no effect outside a Git repository.
Note that --index could be implied by other options such as --3way.

option.name: --no-3way
tip: Disable --3way.

option.name: --no-add
tip: When applying a patch, ignore additions made by the patch.
This can be used to extract the common part between two files by first running diff on them and applying the result with this option, which would apply the deletion part but not the addition part.

option.name: --no-allow-binary-replacement
tip: Disable --allow-binary-replacement.

option.name: --no-allow-empty
tip: Disable --allow-empty.

option.name: --no-apply
tip: Disable --apply.

option.name: --no-binary
tip: Disable --binary.

option.name: --no-cached
tip: Disable --cached.

option.name: --no-check
tip: Disable --check.

option.name: --no-ignore-space-change
tip: Disable --ignore-space-change.

option.name: --no-ignore-whitespace
tip: Disable --ignore-whitespace.

option.name: --no-inaccurate-eof
tip: Disable --inaccurate-eof.

option.name: --no-index
tip: Disable --index.

option.name: --no-intent-to-add
tip: Disable --intent-to-add.

option.name: --no-numstat
tip: Disable --numstat.

option.name: --no-quiet
tip: Disable --quiet.

option.name: --no-recount
tip: Disable --recount.

option.name: --no-reject
tip: Disable --reject.

option.name: --no-reverse
tip: Disable --reverse.

option.name: --no-stat
tip: Disable --stat.

option.name: --no-summary
tip: Disable --summary.

option.name: --no-unidiff-zero
tip: Disable --unidiff-zero.

option.name: --no-unsafe-paths
tip: Disable --unsafe-paths.

option.name: --no-verbose
tip: Disable --verbose.

option.name: --numstat
tip: Similar to --stat, but shows the number of added and deleted lines in decimal notation and the pathname without abbreviation, to make it more machine friendly.
For binary files, outputs two - instead of saying 0 0.
Turns off "apply".

option.name: --ours
tip: Instead of leaving conflicts in the file, resolve conflicts favouring our (or their or both) side of the lines.
Requires --3way.

option.name: --quiet
tip: Suppress stderr output.
Messages about patch status and progress will not be printed.

option.name: --recount
tip: Do not trust the line counts in the hunk headers, but infer them by inspecting the patch (e.g. after editing the patch without adjusting the hunk headers appropriately).

option.name: --reject
tip: For atomicity, git apply by default fails the whole patch and does not touch the working tree when some of the hunks do not apply.
This option makes it apply the parts of the patch that are applicable, and leave the rejected hunks in corresponding *.rej files.

option.name: --reverse
tip: Apply the patch in reverse.

option.name: --stat
tip: Instead of applying the patch, output diffstat for the input.
Turns off "apply".

option.name: --summary
tip: Instead of applying the patch, output a condensed summary of information obtained from git diff extended headers, such as creations, renames, and mode changes.
Turns off "apply".

option.name: --theirs
tip: Instead of leaving conflicts in the file, resolve conflicts favouring our (or their or both) side of the lines.
Requires --3way.

option.name: --unidiff-zero
tip: By default, git apply expects that the patch being applied is a unified diff with at least one line of context.
This provides good safety measures, but breaks down when applying a diff generated with --unified=0.
To bypass these checks use --unidiff-zero.

option.name: --union
tip: Instead of leaving conflicts in the file, resolve conflicts favouring our (or their or both) side of the lines.
Requires --3way.

option.name: --unsafe-paths
tip: By default, a patch that affects outside the working area (either a Git controlled working tree, or the current working directory when git apply is used as a replacement of GNU patch) is rejected as a mistake (or a mischief).

option.name: --verbose
tip: Report progress to stderr.
By default, only a message about the current patch being applied will be printed.
This option will cause additional information to be reported.

option.name: --whitespace
tip: When applying a patch, detect a new or modified line that has whitespace errors.
What are considered whitespace errors is controlled by core.whitespace configuration.

By default, trailing whitespaces (including lines that solely consist of whitespaces) and a space character that is immediately followed by a tab character inside the initial indent of the line are considered whitespace errors.

next.name: error
tip: Treat whitespace errors as errors.

next.name: error-all
tip: Treat all whitespace errors as errors.

next.name: fix
tip: Fix whitespace errors.

next.name: nowarn
tip: Do not warn about whitespace errors.

next.name: warn
tip: Warn about whitespace errors.

option.name: -C
tip: Ensure at least <n> lines of surrounding context match before and after each change.
When fewer lines of surrounding context exist they all must match.
By default no context is ever ignored.

option.name: -p
tip: Remove <n> leading path components (separated by slashes) from traditional diff paths.
E.g., with -p2, a patch against a/dir/file will be applied directly to file.
The default is 1.

option.name: -z
tip: When --numstat has been given, do not munge pathnames, but use a NUL-terminated machine-readable format.

next.name: archimport
tip: Import an Arch repository into Git.

option.name: -a
tip: Attempt to auto-register archives at http://mirrors.sourcecontrol.net This is particularly useful with the -D option.

option.name: -D
tip: Follow merge ancestry and attempt to import trees that have been merged from.
Specify a depth greater than 1 if patch logs have been pruned.

option.name: -f
tip: Use the fast patchset import strategy.
This can be significantly faster for large trees, but cannot handle directory renames or permissions changes.
The default strategy is slow and safe.

option.name: -h
tip: Display usage.

option.name: -o
tip: Use this for compatibility with old-style branch names used by earlier versions of git archimport.
Old-style branch names were category--branch, whereas new-style branch names are archive,category--branch--version.
In both cases, names given on the command-line will override the automatically-generated ones.

option.name: -t
tip: Override the default tempdir.

option.name: -T
tip: Many tags.
Will create a tag for every commit, reflecting the commit name in the Arch repository.

option.name: -v
tip: Verbose output.

next.name: archive
tip: Create a file archive from a named tree.

option.name: --add-file
tip: Add a non-tracked file to the archive.
Can be repeated to add multiple files.
The path of the file in the archive is built by concatenating the value of the last --prefix option (if any) before this --add-file and the basename of <file>.

option.name: --add-virtual-file
tip: Add the specified contents to the archive.
Can be repeated to add multiple files.

option.name: --exec
tip: Used with --remote to specify the path to the git-upload-archive on the remote side.

option.name: --format
tip: Format of the resulting archive.
Possible values are tar, zip, tar.gz, tgz, and any format defined using the configuration option tar.<format>.command.
If --format is not given, and the output file is specified, the format is inferred from the filename if possible (e.g. writing to foo.zip makes the output to be in the zip format).
Otherwise the output format is tar.

option.name: --list
tip: Show all available formats.

option.name: --mtime
tip: Set modification time of archive entries.
Without this option the committer time is used if <tree-ish> is a commit or tag, and the current time if it is a tree.

option.name: --no-list
tip: Disable --list.

option.name: --no-verbose
tip: Disable --verbose.

option.name: --no-worktree-attributes
tip: Disable --worktree-attributes.

option.name: --output
tip: Write the archive to <file> instead of stdout.

option.name: --prefix
tip: Prepend <prefix>/ to paths in the archive.
Can be repeated; its rightmost value is used for all tracked files.

option.name: --remote
tip: Instead of making a tar archive from the local repository, retrieve a tar archive from a remote repository.
Note that the remote repository may place restrictions on which sha1 expressions may be allowed in <tree-ish>.
See git-upload-archive(1) for details.

option.name: --verbose
tip: Report progress to stderr.

option.name: --worktree-attributes

option.name: --filter

tip: Disable --interactive.

tip: Make a bare Git repository.
That is, instead of creating <directory> and placing the administrative files in <directory>/.git, make the <directory> itself the $GIT_DIR.

Also the branch heads at the remote are copied directly to corresponding local branch heads, without mapping them to refs/remotes/origin/.

If multiple values are given for the same key, each value will be written to the config file.
This makes it safe, for example, to add additional fetch refspecs to the origin remote.

option.name: --depth

Clone only the latest commit without historical commit records.

option.name: --fixup
tip: Create a new commit which "fixes up" <commit> when applied with git rebase --autosquash.

Plain --fixup=<commit> creates a "fixup!" commit which changes the content of <commit> but leaves its log message untouched. --fixup=amend:<commit> is similar but creates an "amend!" commit which also replaces the log message of <commit> with the log message of the "amend!" commit. --fixup=reword:<commit> creates an "amend!" commit which replaces the log message of <commit> with its own log message but makes no changes to the content of <commit>.

option.name: --gpg-sign
tip: GPG-sign commits.

The <key-id> is optional and defaults to the committer identity; if specified, it must be stuck to the option without a space. --no-gpg-sign is useful to countermand both commit.gpgSign configuration variable, and earlier --gpg-sign.

option.name: --include
tip: Before making a commit out of staged contents so far, stage the contents of paths given on the command line as well.
This is usually not what you want unless you are concluding a conflicted merge.

option.name: --inter-hunk-context
tip: Show the context between diff hunks, up to the specified <number> of lines, thereby fusing hunks that are close to each other.
Defaults to diff.interHunkContext or 0 if the config option is unset.

option.name: --long
tip: When doing a dry-run, give the output in the long-format.

option.name: --message
tip: Use <msg> as the commit message.
If multiple -m options are given, their values are concatenated as separate paragraphs.

option.name: --no-edit
tip: Use the selected commit message without launching an editor.
For example, git commit --amend --no-edit amends a commit without changing its commit message.

option.name: --no-gpg-sign
tip: GPG-sign commits.

The <key-id> is optional and defaults to the committer identity; if specified, it must be stuck to the option without a space. --no-gpg-sign is useful to countermand both commit.gpgSign configuration variable, and earlier --gpg-sign.

option.name: --no-signoff
tip: Add a Signed-off-by trailer by the committer at the end of the commit log message.
The meaning of a signoff depends on the project to which you're committing.
For example, it may certify that the committer has the rights to submit the work under the project's license or agrees to some contributor representation, such as a Developer Certificate of Origin.

(See https://developercertificate.org for the one used by the Linux kernel and Git projects.) Consult the documentation or leadership of the project to which you're contributing to understand how the signoffs are used in that project.

tip: Do not include the output of git-status(1) in the commit message template when using an editor to prepare the default commit message.

option.name: --no-verbose
tip: Disable --verbose.

option.name: --no-verify
tip: Bypass the pre-commit and commit-msg hooks.
See also githooks(5).

option.name: --null
tip: When showing short or porcelain git-status(1) output, print the filename verbatim and terminate the entries with NUL, instead of LF.
If no format is given, implies the --porcelain output format.
Without the -z option, filenames with "unusual" characters are quoted as explained for the configuration variable core.quotePath (see git-config(1)).

option.name: --only
tip: Make a commit by taking the updated working tree contents of the paths specified on the command line, disregarding any contents that have been staged for other paths.
This is the default mode of operation of git commit if any paths are given on the command line, in which case this option can be omitted.
If this option is specified together with --amend, then no paths need to be specified, which can be used to amend the last commit without committing changes that have already been staged.
If used together with --allow-empty paths are also not required, and an empty commit will be created.

option.name: --patch
tip: Use the interactive patch selection interface to choose which changes to commit.
See git-add(1) for details.

option.name: --pathspec-file-nul
tip: Only meaningful with --pathspec-from-file.
Pathspec elements are separated with NUL character and all other characters are taken literally (including newlines and quotes).

option.name: --pathspec-from-file
tip: Pass pathspec in <file> instead of commandline args.
If <file> is exactly - then standard input is used.
Pathspec elements are separated by LF or CR/LF.
Pathspec elements can be quoted as explained for the configuration variable core.quotePath (see git-config(1)).

option.name: --porcelain
tip: When doing a dry-run, give the output in a porcelain-ready format.
See git-status(1) for details.
Implies --dry-run.

option.name: --quiet
tip: Suppress commit summary message.

option.name: --reedit-message
tip: Like -C, but with -c the editor is invoked, so that the user can further edit the commit message.

option.name: --reset-author
tip: When used with -C/-c/--amend options, or when committing after a conflicting cherry-pick, declare that the authorship of the resulting commit now belongs to the committer.
This also renews the author timestamp.

option.name: --reuse-message
tip: Take an existing <commit> object, and reuse the log message and the authorship information (including the timestamp) when creating the commit.

option.name: --short
tip: When doing a dry-run, give the output in the short-format.
See git-status(1) for details.
Implies --dry-run.

option.name: --signoff
tip: Add a Signed-off-by trailer by the committer at the end of the commit log message.
The meaning of a signoff depends on the project to which you're committing.
For example, it may certify that the committer has the rights to submit the work under the project's license or agrees to some contributor representation, such as a Developer Certificate of Origin.

(See https://developercertificate.org for the one used by the Linux kernel and Git projects.) Consult the documentation or leadership of the project to which you're contributing to understand how the signoffs are used in that project.

option.name: --squash
tip: Construct a commit message for use with git rebase --autosquash.
The commit message title is taken from the specified commit with a prefix of "squash!
Can be used with additional commit message options (-m/-c/-C/-F).

option.name: --status
tip: Include the output of git-status(1) in the commit message template when using an editor to prepare the commit message.
Defaults to on, but can be used to override configuration variable commit.status.

option.name: --template
tip: When editing the commit message, start the editor with the contents in <file>.

This mechanism can be used by projects that want to guide participants with some hints on what to write in the message in what order.

tip: Specify a (<token>, <value>) pair that should be applied as a trailer.

(e.g. git commit --trailer "Signed-off-by:C O Mitter \ <committer@example.com>" --trailer "Helped-by:C O Mitter \ <committer@example.com>" will add the Signed-off-by trailer and the Helped-by trailer to the commit message.) option.name: --unified
tip: Generate diffs with <n> lines of context.
The number of context lines defaults to diff.context or 3 if the configuration variable is unset.
(-U without <n> is silently accepted as a synonym for -p due to a historical accident).

option.name: -l
tip: The -M and -C options involve some preliminary steps that can detect subsets of renames/copies cheaply, followed by an exhaustive fallback portion that compares all remaining unpaired destinations to all relevant sources.
(For renames, only remaining unpaired sources are relevant; for copies, all original sources are relevant.) For N sources and destinations, this exhaustive check is O(N^2).
This option prevents the exhaustive portion of rename/copy detection from running if the number of source/destination files involved exceeds the specified number.
Defaults to diff.renameLimit.

Any combination of the filter characters (including none) can be used.

When * (All-or-none) is added to the combination, all paths are selected if there is any file that matches other criteria in the comparison; if there is no file that matches other criteria, nothing is selected.

If <n> is specified, it is a threshold on the similarity index (i.e. amount of addition/deletions compared to the file's size).
For example, -M90% means Git should consider a delete/add pair to be a rename if more than 90% of the file hasn't changed.
Without a % sign, the number is to be read as a fraction, with a decimal point before it.

option.name: --ignore-cr-at-eol

tip: Treat the <string> given to -S as an extended POSIX regular expression to match.

option.name: --quiet
tip: Disable all output of the program.

option.name: --raw
tip: Generate the diff in raw format.

option.name: --relative
tip: When run from a subdirectory of the project, it can be told to exclude changes outside the directory and show pathnames relative to it with this option.

When you are not in a subdirectory (e.g. in a bare repository), you can name which subdirectory to make the output relative to by giving a <path> as an argument. --no-relative can be used to countermand both diff.relative config option and previous --relative.

option.name: --rename-empty
tip: Whether to use empty blobs as rename source.

option.name: --rotate-to
tip: Discard the files before the named <file> from the output (i.e. skip to), or move them to the end of the output (i.e. rotate to).
These options were invented primarily for the use of the git difftool command, and may not be very useful otherwise.

option.name: --shortstat
tip: Output only the last line of the --stat format containing total number of modified files, as well as number of added and deleted lines.

option.name: --skip-to
tip: Discard the files before the named <file> from the output (i.e. skip to), or move them to the end of the output (i.e. rotate to).

option.name: --src-prefix

option.name: --stat
tip: Generate a diffstat.

Maximum width defaults to terminal width, or 80 columns if not connected to a terminal, and can be overridden by <width>.
The width of the filename part can be limited by giving another width <name-width> after a comma or by setting diff.statNameWidth=<name-width>.

option.name: --stat-count
tip: Limit --stat output to the first <count> lines, followed by ... if there are more.

option.name: --stat-graph-width

option.name: --stat-name-width
tip: Limit the width of the filename part in --stat output.

option.name: --stat-width
tip: Limit the total width in --stat output.

option.name: --submodule
tip: Specify how differences in submodules are shown.
When specifying --submodule=short the short format is used.
This format just shows the names of the commits at the beginning and end of the range.
When --submodule or --submodule=log is specified, the log format is used.

next.name: log

next.name: short

option.name: --summary

option.name: --text

tip: Allow (or disallow) external text conversion filters to be run when comparing binary files.

option.name: --exit-code

option.name: --histogram

option.name: --ignore-cr-at-eol

option.name: --ignore-space-at-eol

Exits with non-zero status if problems are found.

option.name: --color
tip: Show colored diff. --color (i.e. without =<when>) is the same as --color=always. <when> can be one of always, never, or auto.

next.name: always
tip: Always use colors.

next.name: auto
tip: Use colors if terminal supports them.

next.name: never
tip: Never use colors.

option.name: --color-moved
tip: Moved lines of code are colored differently.
The <mode> defaults to no if the option is not given and to zebra if the option with no mode is given.
The mode must be one of:

option.name: --color-moved-ws
tip: This configures how whitespace is ignored when performing the move detection for --color-moved.
These modes can be given as a comma separated list:

option.name: --color-words
tip: Equivalent to --word-diff=color plus (if a regex was specified) --word-diff-regex=<regex>.

option.name: --combined-all-paths
tip: This flag causes combined diffs (used for merge commits) to list the name of the file from all parents.
It thus only has effect when -c or --cc are specified, and is likely only useful if filename changes are detected (i.e. when either rename or copy detection have been requested).

option.name: --commit-list-format
tip: Format to use for the commit list in format-patch.
This option is only relevant when using format-patch.

option.name: --compact-summary
tip: Output a condensed summary of extended header information such as file creations or deletions ("new" or "gone", optionally +l if it's a symlink) and mode changes (+x or -x for adding or removing executable bit respectively) in diffstat.
The information is put between the filename part and the graph part.
Implies --stat.

option.name: --cumulative
tip: Synonym for --dirstat=cumulative.

option.name: --date
tip: Only takes effect for dates shown in human-readable format, such as when using --pretty.
log.date config variable sets a default value for the log command's --date option.

option.name: --decorate
tip: Print out references (branch and tag names) that point at the shown commits.

option.name: --default-prefix
tip: Use the default source and destination prefixes ("a/" and "b/").
This overrides configuration variables such as diff.noprefix, diff.srcPrefix, diff.dstPrefix, and diff.mnemonicPrefix (see git-config(1)).

option.name: --diff-algorithm
tip: Choose a diff algorithm.
The variants are as follows:

next.name: histogram
tip: Use histogram diff algorithm.

next.name: minimal
tip: Use minimal diff algorithm.

next.name: myers
tip: Use Myers diff algorithm (default).

next.name: patience
tip: Use patience diff algorithm.

option.name: --diff-filter
tip: Select only files that are Added (A), Copied (C), Deleted (D), Modified (M), Renamed (R), have their type (i.e. regular file, symlink, submodule, ...:) changed (T), are Unmerged (U), are Unknown (X), or have had their pairing Broken (B).
Any combination of the filter characters (including none) can be used.

When * (All-or-none) is added to the combination, all paths are selected if there is any file that matches other criteria in the comparison; if there is no file that matches other criteria, nothing is selected.

option.name: --dirstat
tip: Output the distribution of relative amount of changes for each sub-directory.
The behavior of --dirstat can be customized by passing it a comma separated list of parameters.
The defaults are controlled by the diff.dirstat configuration variable (see git-config(1)).
The following parameters are available:

option.name: --dirstat-by-file
tip: Synonym for --dirstat=files,<param>,....

option.name: --dst-prefix
tip: Show the given destination <prefix> instead of "b/".

option.name: --encoding
tip: Commit objects record the character encoding used for the log message in their encoding header; this option can be used to tell the command to re-code the commit log message in the encoding preferred by the user.
For non plumbing commands this defaults to UTF-8.
Note that if an object claims to be encoded in X and we are outputting in X, we will output the object verbatim; this means that invalid sequences in the original commit may be copied to the output.
Likewise, if iconv(3) fails to convert the commit, we will quietly output the original object verbatim.

option.name: --exit-code
tip: Make the program exit with codes similar to diff(1).
That is, it exits with 1 if there were differences and 0 means no differences.

option.name: --expand-tabs
tip: Perform a tab expansion (replace each tab with enough spaces to fill to the next display column that is a multiple of <n>) in the log message before showing it in the output. --expand-tabs is a short-hand for --expand-tabs=8, and --no-expand-tabs is a short-hand for --expand-tabs=0, which disables tab expansion.

option.name: --ext-diff
tip: Allow an external diff helper to be executed.
If you set an external diff driver with gitattributes(5), you need to use this option with git-log(1) and friends.

option.name: --find-copies
tip: Detect copies as well as renames.
See also --find-copies-harder.
If <n> is specified, it has the same meaning as for -M<n>.

option.name: --find-copies-harder
tip: For performance reasons, by default, -C option finds copies only if the original file of the copy was modified in the same changeset.
This flag makes the command inspect unmodified files as candidates for the source of copy.
This is a very expensive operation for large projects, so use it with caution.
Giving more than one -C option has the same effect.

option.name: --find-object
tip: Look for differences that change the number of occurrences of the specified object.
Similar to -S, just the argument is different in that it doesn't search for a specific string but for a specific object id.

option.name: --find-renames
tip: Detect renames.
If <n> is specified, it is a threshold on the similarity index (i.e. amount of addition/deletions compared to the file's size).
For example, -M90% means Git should consider a delete/add pair to be a rename if more than 90% of the file hasn't changed.
Without a % sign, the number is to be read as a fraction, with a decimal point before it.

option.name: --format
tip: Pretty-print the contents of the commit logs in a given format, where <format> can be one of oneline, short, medium, full, fuller, reference, email, raw, format:<string> and tformat:<string>.
When <format> is none of the above, and has %<placeholder> in it, it acts as if --pretty=tformat:<format> were given.

option.name: --full-index
tip: Instead of the first handful of characters, show the full pre- and post-image blob object names on the "index" line when generating patch format output.

option.name: --function-context
tip: Show whole function as context lines for each change.
The function names are determined in the same way as git diff works out patch hunk headers (see "Defining a custom hunk-header" in gitattributes(5)).

option.name: --histogram
tip: Generate a diff using the "histogram diff" algorithm.

option.name: --ignore-all-space
tip: Ignore whitespace when comparing lines.
This ignores differences even if one line has whitespace where the other line has none.

option.name: --ignore-blank-lines
tip: Ignore changes whose lines are all blank.

option.name: --ignore-cr-at-eol
tip: Ignore carriage-return at the end of line when doing a comparison.

option.name: --ignore-matching-lines
tip: Ignore changes whose all lines match <regex>.
This option may be specified more than once.

option.name: --ignore-space-at-eol
tip: Ignore changes in whitespace at EOL.

option.name: --ignore-space-change
tip: Ignore changes in amount of whitespace.
This ignores whitespace at line end, and considers all other sequences of one or more whitespace characters to be equivalent.

option.name: --ignore-submodules
tip: Ignore changes to submodules in the diff generation. all is the default.

Using none will consider the submodule modified when it either contains untracked or modified files or its HEAD differs from the commit recorded in the superproject and can be used to override any settings of the ignore option in git-config(1) or gitmodules(5).
When untracked is used submodules are not considered dirty when they only contain untracked content (but they are still scanned for modified content).
Using dirty ignores all changes to the work tree of submodules, only changes to the commits stored in the superproject are shown (this was the behavior until 1.7.0).

option.name: --indent-heuristic
tip: Enable the heuristic that shifts diff hunk boundaries to make patches easier to read.
This is the default.

option.name: --inter-hunk-context
tip: Show the context between diff hunks, up to the specified <number> of lines, thereby fusing hunks that are close to each other.
Defaults to diff.interHunkContext or 0 if the config option is unset.

option.name: --irreversible-delete
tip: Omit the preimage for deletes, i.e. print only the header but not the diff between the preimage and /dev/null.
The resulting patch is not meant to be applied with patch or git apply; this is solely for people who want to just concentrate on reviewing the text after the change.
In addition, the output obviously lacks enough information to apply such a patch in reverse, even manually, hence the name of the option.

option.name: --ita-invisible-in-index
tip: By default entries added by git add -N appear as an existing empty file in git diff and a new file in git diff --cached.
This option makes the entry appear as a new file in git diff and non-existent in git diff --cached.
This option could be reverted with --ita-visible-in-index.
Both options are experimental and could be removed in future.

option.name: --ita-visible-in-index
tip: By default entries added by git add -N appear as an existing empty file in git diff and a new file in git diff --cached.
This option makes the entry appear as a new file in git diff and non-existent in git diff --cached. This option could be reverted with --ita-invisible-in-index.

option.name: --line-prefix
tip: Prepend an additional <prefix> to every line of output.

option.name: --max-depth
tip: For each pathspec given on command line, descend at most <depth> levels of directories.
A value of -1 means no limit.
Cannot be combined with wildcards in the pathspec.
Given a tree containing foo/bar/baz, the following list shows the matches generated by each set of options:

option.name: --merge-base
tip: Instead of comparing the <tree-ish>s directly, use the merge base between the two <tree-ish>s as the "before" side.
There must be two <tree-ish>s given and they must both be commits.

option.name: --minimal
tip: Spend extra time to make sure the smallest possible diff is produced.

option.name: --name-only
tip: Show only the name of each changed file in the post-image tree.
The file names are often encoded in UTF-8.
For more information see the discussion about encoding in the git-log(1) manual page.

option.name: --name-status
tip: Show only the name(s) and status of each changed file.
See the description of the --diff-filter option on what the status letters mean.
Just like --name-only the file names are often encoded in UTF-8.

option.name: --no-abbrev
tip: Display the full sha1s in the output listing rather than abbreviating them.

option.name: --no-abbrev-commit
tip: Show the full 40-byte hexadecimal commit object name.
This negates --abbrev-commit, either explicit or implied by other options such as --oneline.
It also overrides the log.abbrevCommit variable.

option.name: --no-always
tip: Disable --always.

option.name: --no-binary
tip: Disable --binary.

option.name: --no-cc
tip: Disable --cc.

option.name: --no-check
tip: Disable --check.

option.name: --no-color
tip: Turn off colored diff.
It is the same as --color=never.

option.name: --no-color-moved
tip: Turn off move detection.
This can be used to override configuration settings.
It is the same as --color-moved=no.

option.name: --no-color-moved-ws
tip: Do not ignore whitespace when performing move detection.
This can be used to override configuration settings.
It is the same as --color-moved-ws=no.

option.name: --no-combined-all-paths
tip: Disable --combined-all-paths.

option.name: --no-commit-id
tip: git diff-tree outputs a line with the commit ID when applicable.
This flag suppresses the commit ID output.

option.name: --no-compact-summary
tip: Disable --compact-summary.

option.name: --no-cumulative
tip: Disable --cumulative.

option.name: --no-decorate
tip: Disable --decorate.

option.name: --no-default-prefix
tip: Disable --default-prefix.

option.name: --no-exit-code
tip: Disable --exit-code.

option.name: --no-expand-tabs
tip: Perform a tab expansion (replace each tab with enough spaces to fill to the next display column that is a multiple of <n>) in the log message before showing it in the output. --expand-tabs is a short-hand for --expand-tabs=8, and --no-expand-tabs is a short-hand for --expand-tabs=0, which disables tab expansion.

option.name: --no-ext-diff
tip: Disallow external diff drivers.

option.name: --no-find-copies-harder
tip: Disable --find-copies-harder.

option.name: --no-full-index
tip: Disable --full-index.

option.name: --no-function-context
tip: Disable --function-context.

option.name: --no-histogram
tip: Disable --histogram.

option.name: --no-ignore-all-space
tip: Disable --ignore-all-space.

option.name: --no-ignore-blank-lines
tip: Disable --ignore-blank-lines.

option.name: --no-ignore-cr-at-eol
tip: Disable --ignore-cr-at-eol.

option.name: --no-ignore-space-at-eol
tip: Disable --ignore-space-at-eol.

option.name: --no-ignore-space-change
tip: Disable --ignore-space-change.

option.name: --no-indent-heuristic
tip: Disable the indent heuristic.

option.name: --no-irreversible-delete
tip: Disable --irreversible-delete.

option.name: --no-ita-invisible-in-index
tip: Disable --ita-invisible-in-index.

option.name: --no-ita-visible-in-index
tip: Disable --ita-visible-in-index.

option.name: --no-merge-base
tip: Disable --merge-base.

option.name: --no-minimal
tip: Disable --minimal.

option.name: --no-name-only
tip: Disable --name-only.

option.name: --no-name-status
tip: Disable --name-status.

option.name: --no-notes
tip: Do not show notes.
This negates the above --notes option, by resetting the list of notes refs from which notes are shown.
Options are parsed in the order given on the command line, so e.g. "--notes --notes=foo --no-notes --notes=bar" will only show notes from refs/notes/bar.

option.name: --no-numstat
tip: Disable --numstat.

option.name: --no-oneline
tip: Disable --oneline.

option.name: --no-patch
tip: Suppress all output from the diff machinery.
Useful for commands like git show that show the patch by default to squelch their output, or to cancel the effect of options like --patch, --stat earlier on the command line in an alias.

option.name: --no-patch-with-raw
tip: Disable --patch-with-raw.

option.name: --no-patch-with-stat
tip: Disable --patch-with-stat.

option.name: --no-patience
tip: Disable --patience.

option.name: --no-pickaxe-all
tip: Disable --pickaxe-all.

option.name: --no-pickaxe-regex
tip: Disable --pickaxe-regex.

option.name: --no-prefix
tip: Do not show any source or destination prefix.

option.name: --no-quiet
tip: Disable --quiet.

option.name: --no-raw
tip: Disable --raw.

option.name: --no-relative
tip: When run from a subdirectory of the project, it can be told to exclude changes outside the directory and show pathnames relative to it with this option.

When you are not in a subdirectory (e.g. in a bare repository), you can name which subdirectory to make the output relative to by giving a <path> as an argument. --no-relative can be used to countermand both diff.relative config option and previous --relative.

option.name: --no-rename-empty
tip: Whether to use empty blobs as rename source.

option.name: --no-renames
tip: Turn off rename detection, even when the configuration file gives the default to do so.

option.name: --no-root
tip: Disable --root.

option.name: --no-shortstat
tip: Disable --shortstat.

option.name: --no-show-notes-by-default
tip: Disable --show-notes-by-default.

option.name: --no-show-signature
tip: Disable --show-signature.

option.name: --no-standard-notes
tip: These options are deprecated.
Use the above --notes/--no-notes options instead.

option.name: --no-stdin
tip: Disable --stdin.

option.name: --no-summary
tip: Disable --summary.

option.name: --no-text
tip: Disable --text.

option.name: --no-textconv
tip: Allow (or disallow) external text conversion filters to be run when comparing binary files.
See gitattributes(5) for details.
Because textconv filters are typically a one-way conversion, the resulting diff is suitable for human consumption, but cannot be applied.
For this reason, textconv filters are enabled by default only for git-diff(1) and git-log(1), but not for git-format-patch(1) or diff plumbing commands.

option.name: --notes
tip: Show the notes (see git-notes(1)) that annotate the commit, when showing the commit log message.
This is the default for git log, git show and git whatchanged commands when there is no --pretty, --format, or --oneline option given on the command line.

option.name: --numstat
tip: Similar to --stat, but shows number of added and deleted lines in decimal notation and pathname without abbreviation, to make it more machine friendly.
For binary files, outputs two - instead of saying 0 0.

option.name: --oneline
tip: This is a shorthand for --pretty=oneline --abbrev-commit used together.

option.name: --output
tip: Output to a specific file instead of stdout.

option.name: --output-indicator-context
tip: Specify the character used to indicate new, old or context lines in the generated patch.
Normally they are +, - and ' ' respectively.

option.name: --output-indicator-new
tip: Specify the character used to indicate new, old or context lines in the generated patch.
Normally they are +, - and ' ' respectively.

option.name: --output-indicator-old
tip: Specify the character used to indicate new, old or context lines in the generated patch.
Normally they are +, - and ' ' respectively.

option.name: --patch
tip: Generate patch (see the section called "GENERATING PATCH TEXT WITH -P").

option.name: --patch-with-raw
tip: Synonym for -p --raw.

option.name: --patch-with-stat
tip: Synonym for -p --stat.

option.name: --patience
tip: Generate a diff using the "patience diff" algorithm.

option.name: --pickaxe-all
tip: When -S or -G finds a change, show all the changes in that changeset, not just the files that contain the change in <string>.

option.name: --pickaxe-regex
tip: Treat the <string> given to -S as an extended POSIX regular expression to match.

option.name: --pretty
tip: Pretty-print the contents of the commit logs in a given format, where <format> can be one of oneline, short, medium, full, fuller, reference, email, raw, format:<string> and tformat:<string>.
When <format> is none of the above, and has %<placeholder> in it, it acts as if --pretty=tformat:<format> were given.

option.name: --quiet
tip: Disable all output of the program.
Implies --exit-code.

Disables execution of external diff helpers whose exit code is not trusted, i.e. their respective configuration option diff.trustExitCode or diff.<driver>.trustExitCode or environment variable GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF_TRUST_EXIT_CODE is false.

option.name: --raw
tip: Generate the diff in raw format.
This is the default.

option.name: --relative
tip: When run from a subdirectory of the project, it can be told to exclude changes outside the directory and show pathnames relative to it with this option.

When you are not in a subdirectory (e.g. in a bare repository), you can name which subdirectory to make the output relative to by giving a <path> as an argument. --no-relative can be used to countermand both diff.relative config option and previous --relative.

option.name: --rename-empty
tip: Whether to use empty blobs as rename source.

option.name: --root
tip: When --root is specified the initial commit will be shown as a big creation event.
This is equivalent to a diff against the NULL tree.

option.name: --rotate-to
tip: Discard the files before the named <file> from the output (i.e. skip to), or move them to the end of the output (i.e. rotate to).
These options were invented primarily for the use of the git difftool command, and may not be very useful otherwise.

option.name: --shortstat
tip: Output only the last line of the --stat format containing total number of modified files, as well as number of added and deleted lines.

option.name: --show-notes
tip: These options are deprecated.
Use the above --notes/--no-notes options instead.

option.name: --show-notes-by-default
tip: Show the default notes unless options for displaying specific notes are given.

option.name: --show-signature
tip: Check the validity of a signed commit object by passing the signature to gpg --verify and show the output.

option.name: --skip-to
tip: Discard the files before the named <file> from the output (i.e. skip to), or move them to the end of the output (i.e. rotate to).
These options were invented primarily for the use of the git difftool command, and may not be very useful otherwise.

option.name: --src-prefix
tip: Show the given source <prefix> instead of "a/".

option.name: --standard-notes
tip: These options are deprecated.
Use the above --notes/--no-notes options instead.

option.name: --stat
tip: Generate a diffstat.
By default, as much space as necessary will be used for the filename part, and the rest for the graph part.
Maximum width defaults to terminal width, or 80 columns if not connected to a terminal, and can be overridden by <width>.
The width of the filename part can be limited by giving another width <name-width> after a comma or by setting diff.statNameWidth=<name-width>.

option.name: --stdin
tip: When --stdin is specified, the command does not take <tree-ish> arguments from the command line.
Instead, it reads lines containing either two <tree>, one <commit>, or a list of <commit> from its standard input.
(Use a single space as separator.)

option.name: --submodule
tip: Specify how differences in submodules are shown.
When specifying --submodule=short the short format is used.
This format just shows the names of the commits at the beginning and end of the range.
When --submodule or --submodule=log is specified, the log format is used.

option.name: --summary
tip: Output a condensed summary of extended header information such as creations, renames and mode changes.

option.name: --text
tip: Treat all files as text.

option.name: --textconv
tip: Allow (or disallow) external text conversion filters to be run when comparing binary files.
See gitattributes(5) for details.
Because textconv filters are typically a one-way conversion, the resulting diff is suitable for human consumption, but cannot be applied.
For this reason, textconv filters are enabled by default only for git-diff(1) and git-log(1), but not for git-format-patch(1) or diff plumbing commands.

option.name: --unified
tip: Generate diffs with <n> lines of context.
The number of context lines defaults to diff.context or 3 if the configuration variable is unset.
(-U without <n> is silently accepted as a synonym for -p due to a historical accident).
Implies --patch.

option.name: --word-diff
tip: By default, words are delimited by whitespace; see --word-diff-regex below.
The <mode> defaults to plain, and must be one of:

option.name: --word-diff-regex
tip: Use <regex> to decide what a word is, instead of considering runs of non-whitespace to be a word.
Also implies --word-diff unless it was already enabled.

option.name: --ws-error-highlight
tip: Highlight whitespace errors in the context, old or new lines of the diff.
Multiple values are separated by comma, none resets previous values, default reset the list to new and all is a shorthand for old,new,context.
When this option is not given, and the configuration variable diff.wsErrorHighlight is not set, only whitespace errors in new lines are highlighted.
The whitespace errors are colored with color.diff.whitespace.

option.name: -c
tip: This flag changes the way a merge commit is displayed (which means it is useful only when the command is given one <tree-ish>, or --stdin).
It shows the differences from each of the parents to the merge result simultaneously instead of showing pairwise diff between a parent and the result one at a time (which is what the -m option does).
Furthermore, it lists only files which were modified from all parents.

option.name: -G
tip: Look for differences whose patch text contains added/removed lines that match <regex>.

option.name: -l
tip: The -M and -C options involve some preliminary steps that can detect subsets of renames/copies cheaply, followed by an exhaustive fallback portion that compares all remaining unpaired destinations to all relevant sources.
(For renames, only remaining unpaired sources are relevant; for copies, all original sources are relevant.) For N sources and destinations, this exhaustive check is O(N^2).
This option prevents the exhaustive portion of rename/copy detection from running if the number of source/destination files involved exceeds the specified number.
Defaults to diff.renameLimit.

option.name: -m
tip: By default, git diff-tree --stdin does not show differences for merge commits.
With this flag, it shows differences to that commit from all of its parents.
See also -c.

option.name: -O
tip: Control the order in which files appear in the output.
This overrides the diff.orderFile configuration variable (see git-config(1)).
To cancel diff.orderFile, use -O/dev/null.

option.name: -r
tip: Recurse into sub-trees.

option.name: -R
tip: Swap two inputs; that is, show differences from index or on-disk file to tree contents.

option.name: -S
tip: Look for differences that change the number of occurrences of the specified <string> (i.e. addition/deletion) in a file.
Intended for the scripter's use.

option.name: -t
tip: Show tree entry itself as well as subtrees.
Implies -r.

option.name: -v
tip: This flag causes git diff-tree --stdin to also show the commit message before the differences.

option.name: -z
tip: When --raw, --numstat, --name-only or --name-status has been given, do not munge pathnames and use NULs as output field terminators.

next.name: difftool
tip: Display changes using common diff tools.

option.name: --dir-diff
tip: Copy the modified files to a temporary location and perform a directory diff on them.
This mode never prompts before launching the diff tool.

option.name: --extcmd
tip: Specify a custom command for viewing diffs. git-difftool ignores the configured defaults and runs <command> $LOCAL $REMOTE when this option is specified.
Additionally, $BASE is set in the environment.

option.name: --gui
tip: When git-difftool is invoked with the -g or --gui option the default diff tool will be read from the configured diff.guitool variable instead of diff.tool.
This may be selected automatically using the configuration variable difftool.guiDefault.
The --no-gui option can be used to override these settings.
If diff.guitool is not set, we will fallback in the order of merge.guitool, diff.tool, merge.tool until a tool is found.

option.name: --no-dir-diff
tip: Disable --dir-diff.

option.name: --no-gui
tip: When git-difftool is invoked with the -g or --gui option the default diff tool will be read from the configured diff.guitool variable instead of diff.tool.
This may be selected automatically using the configuration variable difftool.guiDefault.
The --no-gui option can be used to override these settings.
If diff.guitool is not set, we will fallback in the order of merge.guitool, diff.tool, merge.tool until a tool is found.

option.name: --no-prompt
tip: Do not prompt before launching a diff tool.

option.name: --no-symlinks
tip: git difftool's default behavior is to create symlinks to the working tree when run in --dir-diff mode and the right-hand side of the comparison yields the same content as the file in the working tree.

option.name: --no-tool-help
tip: Disable --tool-help.

option.name: --no-trust-exit-code
tip: Errors reported by the diff tool are ignored by default.
Use --trust-exit-code to make git-difftool exit when an invoked diff tool returns a non-zero exit code.

option.name: --prompt

option.name: --negotiation-restrict

option.name: --negotiation-tip
tip: By default, Git will report, to the server, commits reachable from all local refs to find common commits in an attempt to reduce the size of the to-be-received packfile.
If specified, Git will only report commits reachable from the given tips.
This is useful to speed up fetches when the user knows which local ref is likely to have commits in common with the upstream ref being fetched.

option.name: --porcelain

tip: Modify the configured refspec to place all refs into the refs/prefetch/ namespace.

option.name: --progress
tip: Progress status is reported on the standard error stream by default when it is attached to a terminal, unless -q is specified.
This flag forces progress status even if the standard error stream is not directed to a terminal.

option.name: --prune
tip: Before fetching, remove any remote-tracking references that no longer exist on the remote.
Tags are not subject to pruning if they are fetched only because of the default tag auto-following or due to a --tags option.

However, if tags are fetched due to an explicit refspec (either on the command line or in the remote configuration, for example if the remote was cloned with the --mirror option), then they are also subject to pruning.
Supplying --prune-tags is a shorthand for providing the tag refspec.

option.name: --prune-tags
tip: Before fetching, remove any local tags that no longer exist on the remote if --prune is enabled.
This option should be used more carefully, unlike --prune it will remove any local references (local tags) that have been created.
This option is a shorthand for providing the explicit tag refspec along with --prune, see the discussion about that in its documentation.

option.name: --quiet

option.name: --recurse-submodules
tip: Control if and under what conditions new commits of submodules should be fetched too.

When recursing through submodules, git fetch always attempts to fetch "changed" submodules, that is, a submodule that has commits that are referenced by a newly fetched superproject commit but are missing in the local submodule clone.

A changed submodule can be fetched as long as it is present locally e.g. in $GIT_DIR/modules/ (see gitsubmodules(7)); if the upstream adds a new submodule, that submodule cannot be fetched until it is cloned e.g. by git submodule update.

option.name: --recurse-submodules-default

See section on "Configured Remote-tracking Branches" for details.

option.name: --set-upstream

option.name: --shallow-exclude

option.name: --shallow-since
