Can be given multiple times.

option.name: --trim-empty
tip: If the <value> part of any trailer contains only whitespace, the whole trailer will be removed from the output.
This applies to existing trailers as well as new trailers.

option.name: --unfold
tip: If a trailer has a value that runs over multiple lines (aka "folded"), reformat the value into a single line.
The default is --no-unfold.

option.name: --where
tip: Specify where all new trailers will be added.

A setting provided with --where overrides the trailer.where and any applicable trailer.<key-alias>.where configuration variables and applies to all --trailer options until the next occurrence of --where or --no-where.
Possible placements are after, before, end or start.

next.name: after
tip: Add after existing trailers.

next.name: before
tip: Add before existing trailers.

next.name: end
tip: Add at the end.

next.name: start
tip: Add at the start.

next.name: jump
tip: Jump to interesting elements in an editor.

next.name: last-modified
tip: EXPERIMENTAL: Show when files were last modified.

option.name: --max-depth
tip: Traverse at most <depth> levels into subtrees.

option.name: --no-recursive
tip: Disable --recursive.

option.name: --no-show-trees
tip: Disable --show-trees.

option.name: --recursive
tip: Recursively traverse into all subtrees.

option.name: --show-trees
tip: Show tree entries even when recursing into them.

option.name: -z
tip: Terminate each line with a NUL character rather than a newline.

next.name: lfs
tip: Work with large files in Git repositories.

next.name: checkout
tip: Populate working copy with real content from Git LFS files.

next.name: completion
tip: Generate shell scripts for command-line tab-completion of Git LFS commands.

next.name: dedup
tip: De-duplicate Git LFS files.

next.name: env
tip: Display the Git LFS environment.

next.name: ext
tip: Display Git LFS extension details.

next.name: fetch
tip: Download Git LFS files from a remote.

next.name: fsck
tip: Check Git LFS files for consistency.

next.name: install
tip: Install Git LFS configuration.

next.name: lock
tip: Set a file as "locked" on the Git LFS server.

next.name: locks
tip: List currently "locked" files from the Git LFS server.

next.name: logs
tip: Show errors from the Git LFS command.

next.name: ls-files
tip: Show information about Git LFS files in the index and working tree.

next.name: migrate
tip: Migrate history to or from Git LFS.

next.name: prune
tip: Delete old Git LFS files from local storage.

next.name: pull
tip: Fetch Git LFS changes from the remote & checkout any required working tree files.

next.name: push
tip: Push queued large files to the Git LFS endpoint.

next.name: status
tip: Show the status of Git LFS files in the working tree.

next.name: track
tip: View or add Git LFS paths to Git attributes.

next.name: uninstall
tip: Uninstall Git LFS by removing hooks and smudge/clean filter configuration.

next.name: unlock
tip: Remove "locked" setting for a file on the Git LFS server.

next.name: untrack
tip: Remove Git LFS paths from Git Attributes.

next.name: update
tip: Update Git hooks for the current Git repository.

next.name: version
tip: Report the version number.

next.name: log
tip: Show commit logs.

option.name: --abbrev
tip: Instead of showing the full 40-byte hexadecimal object name in diff-raw format output and diff-tree header lines, show the shortest prefix that is at least <n> hexdigits long that uniquely refers the object.
In diff-patch output format, --full-index takes higher precedence, i.e. if --full-index is specified, full blob names will be shown regardless of --abbrev.
Non default number of digits can be specified with --abbrev=<n>.

option.name: --abbrev-commit
tip: Instead of showing the full 40-byte hexadecimal commit object name, show a prefix that names the object uniquely. --abbrev=<n> (which also modifies diff output, if it is displayed) option can be used to specify the minimum length of the prefix.

option.name: --after
tip: Show commits more recent than <date>.
As a special case, today means the last midnight.

option.name: --all
tip: Pretend as if all the refs in refs/, along with HEAD, are listed on the command line as <commit>.

option.name: --all-match
tip: Limit the commits output to ones that match all given --grep, instead of ones that match at least one.

option.name: --alternate-refs
tip: Pretend as if all objects mentioned as ref tips of alternate repositories were listed on the command line.
An alternate repository is any repository whose object directory is specified in objects/info/alternates.
The set of included objects may be modified by core.alternateRefsCommand, etc. See git-config(1).

option.name: --ancestry-path
tip: When given a range of commits to display (e.g. <commit1>..<commit2> or <commit2> ^<commit1>), and a commit <commit> in that range, only display commits in that range that are ancestors of <commit>, descendants of <commit>, or <commit> itself.
If no commit is specified, use <commit1> (the excluded part of the range) as <commit>.
Can be passed multiple times; if so, a commit is included if it is any of the commits given or if it is an ancestor or descendant of one of them.

option.name: --anchored
tip: Generate a diff using the "anchored diff" algorithm.

option.name: --author
tip: Limit the commits output to ones with author/committer header lines that match the <pattern> regular expression.
With more than one --author=<pattern>, commits whose author matches any of the <pattern> are chosen (similarly for multiple --committer=<pattern>).

option.name: --author-date-order
tip: Show no parents before all of its children are shown, but otherwise show commits in the author timestamp order.

option.name: --basic-regexp
tip: Consider the limiting patterns to be basic regular expressions; this is the default.

option.name: --before
tip: Show commits older than <date>.

option.name: --binary
tip: In addition to --full-index, output a binary diff that can be applied with git-apply.
Implies --patch.

option.name: --bisect
tip: Pretend as if the bad bisection ref refs/bisect/bad was listed and as if it was followed by --not and the good bisection refs refs/bisect/good-* on the command line.

option.name: --boundary
tip: Output excluded boundary commits.
Boundary commits are prefixed with -.

option.name: --branches
tip: Pretend as if all the refs in refs/heads are listed on the command line as <commit>.
If <pattern> is given, limit branches to ones matching given shell glob.
If <pattern> lacks ?, *, or [, /* at the end is implied.

option.name: --break-rewrites
tip: Break complete rewrite changes into pairs of delete and create.
This serves two purposes:

option.name: --cc
tip: Produce dense combined diff output for merge commits.
Shortcut for --diff-merges=dense-combined -p.

option.name: --check
tip: Warn if changes introduce conflict markers or whitespace errors.
What are considered whitespace errors is controlled by core.whitespace configuration.

By default, trailing whitespaces (including lines that consist solely of whitespaces) and a space character that is immediately followed by a tab character inside the initial indent of the line are considered whitespace errors.
Exits with non-zero status if problems are found.

option.name: --cherry
tip: A synonym for --right-only --cherry-mark --no-merges; useful to limit the output to the commits on our side and mark those that have been applied to the other side of a forked history with git log --cherry upstream...mybranch, similar to git cherry upstream mybranch.

option.name: --cherry-mark
tip: Like --cherry-pick (see below) but mark equivalent commits with = rather than omitting them, and inequivalent ones with +.

option.name: --cherry-pick
tip: Omit any commit that introduces the same change as another commit on the "other side" when the set of commits are limited with symmetric difference.

option.name: --children
tip: Print also the children of the commit (in the form "commit child...:").
Also enables parent rewriting, see History Simplification above.

option.name: --clear-decorations
tip: When specified, this option clears all previous --decorate-refs or --decorate-refs-exclude options and relaxes the default decoration filter to include all references.
This option is assumed if the config value log.initialDecorationSet is set to all.

option.name: --color
tip: Show colored diff. --color (i.e. without =<when>) is the same as --color=always. <when> can be one of always, never, or auto.

next.name: always
tip: Always use colors.

next.name: auto
tip: Use colors if terminal supports them.

next.name: never
tip: Never use colors.

option.name: --color-moved
tip: Moved lines of code are colored differently.
The <mode> defaults to no if the option is not given and to zebra if the option with no mode is given.
The mode must be one of:

option.name: --color-moved-ws
tip: This configures how whitespace is ignored when performing the move detection for --color-moved.
These modes can be given as a comma separated list:

option.name: --color-words
tip: Equivalent to --word-diff=color plus (if a regex was specified) --word-diff-regex=<regex>.

option.name: --combined-all-paths
tip: Cause combined diffs (used for merge commits) to list the name of the file from all parents.
It thus only has effect when --diff-merges=[dense-]combined is in use, and is likely only useful if filename changes are detected (i.e. when either rename or copy detection have been requested).

option.name: --commit-list-format
tip: Format to use for the commit list in format-patch.
This option is only relevant when using format-patch.

option.name: --committer
tip: Limit the commits output to ones with author/committer header lines that match the <pattern> regular expression.
With more than one --author=<pattern>, commits whose author matches any of the <pattern> are chosen (similarly for multiple --committer=<pattern>).

option.name: --compact-summary
tip: Output a condensed summary of extended header information such as file creations or deletions ("new" or "gone", optionally +l if it's a symlink) and mode changes (+x or -x for adding or removing executable bit respectively) in diffstat.
The information is put between the filename part and the graph part.
Implies --stat.

option.name: --cumulative
tip: Synonym for --dirstat=cumulative.

option.name: --date
tip: Only takes effect for dates shown in human-readable format, such as when using --pretty. log.date config variable sets a default value for the log command's --date option.
By default, dates are shown in the original time zone (either committer's or author's).
If -local is appended to the format (e.g., iso-local), the user's local time zone is used instead.

option.name: --date-order
tip: Show no parents before all of its children are shown, but otherwise show commits in the commit timestamp order.

option.name: --dd
tip: Produce diff with respect to first parent for both merge and regular commits.
Shortcut for --diff-merges=first-parent -p.

option.name: --decorate
tip: Print out the ref names of any commits that are shown.
Possible values are:

option.name: --decorate-refs
tip: For each candidate reference, do not use it for decoration if it matches any of the <pattern> parameters given to --decorate-refs-exclude or if it doesn't match any of the <pattern> parameters given to --decorate-refs.
The log.excludeDecoration config option allows excluding refs from the decorations, but an explicit --decorate-refs pattern will override a match in log.excludeDecoration.

option.name: --decorate-refs-exclude
tip: For each candidate reference, do not use it for decoration if it matches any of the <pattern> parameters given to --decorate-refs-exclude or if it doesn't match any of the <pattern> parameters given to --decorate-refs.
The log.excludeDecoration config option allows excluding refs from the decorations, but an explicit --decorate-refs pattern will override a match in log.excludeDecoration.

option.name: --default-prefix
tip: Use the default source and destination prefixes ("a/" and "b/").
This overrides configuration variables such as diff.noprefix, diff.srcPrefix, diff.dstPrefix, and diff.mnemonicPrefix (see git-config(1)).

option.name: --dense
tip: Only the selected commits are shown, plus some to have a meaningful history.

option.name: --diff-algorithm
tip: Choose a diff algorithm.
The variants are as follows:

next.name: histogram
tip: Use histogram diff algorithm.

next.name: minimal
tip: Use minimal diff algorithm.

next.name: myers
tip: Use Myers diff algorithm (default).

next.name: patience
tip: Use patience diff algorithm.

option.name: --diff-filter
tip: Select only files that are Added (A), Copied (C), Deleted (D), Modified (M), Renamed (R), have their type (i.e. regular file, symlink, submodule, ...:) changed (T), are Unmerged (U), are Unknown (X), or have had their pairing Broken (B).
Any combination of the filter characters (including none) can be used.

When * (All-or-none) is added to the combination, all paths are selected if there is any file that matches other criteria in the comparison; if there is no file that matches other criteria, nothing is selected.

option.name: --diff-merges
tip: Specify diff format to be used for merge commits.
Default is `off` unless --first-parent is in use, in which case first-parent is the default.

option.name: --dirstat
tip: Output the distribution of relative amount of changes for each sub-directory.
The behavior of --dirstat can be customized by passing it a comma separated list of parameters.
The defaults are controlled by the diff.dirstat configuration variable (see git-config(1)).
The following parameters are available:

option.name: --dirstat-by-file
tip: Synonym for --dirstat=files,<param>,....

option.name: --do-walk
tip: Overrides a previous --no-walk.

option.name: --dst-prefix
tip: Show the given destination <prefix> instead of "b/".

option.name: --encoding
tip: Commit objects record the character encoding used for the log message in their encoding header; this option can be used to tell the command to re-code the commit log message in the encoding preferred by the user.
For non plumbing commands this defaults to UTF-8.
Note that if an object claims to be encoded in X and we are outputting in X, we will output the object verbatim; this means that invalid sequences in the original commit may be copied to the output.
Likewise, if iconv(3) fails to convert the commit, we will quietly output the original object verbatim.

option.name: --exclude
tip: Do not include refs matching <glob-pattern> that the next --all, --branches, --tags, --remotes, or --glob would otherwise consider.
Repetitions of this option accumulate exclusion patterns up to the next --all, --branches, --tags, --remotes, or --glob option (other options or arguments do not clear accumulated patterns).

option.name: --exclude-first-parent-only
tip: When finding commits to exclude (with a ^), follow only the first parent commit upon seeing a merge commit.
This can be used to find the set of changes in a topic branch from the point where it diverged from the remote branch, given that arbitrary merges can be valid topic branch changes.

option.name: --exclude-hidden
tip: Do not include refs that would be hidden by git-fetch, git-receive-pack or git-upload-pack by consulting the appropriate fetch.hideRefs, receive.hideRefs or uploadpack.hideRefs configuration along with transfer.hideRefs (see git-config(1)).
This option affects the next pseudo-ref option --all or --glob and is cleared after processing them.

next.name: fetch
tip: Exclude fetch hidden refs.

next.name: receive
tip: Exclude receive hidden refs.

next.name: uploadpack
tip: Exclude uploadpack hidden refs.

option.name: --exit-code
tip: When there are no commits to display, exit with code 1 instead of 0.
This is useful for scripts that want to detect when there are no commits.

option.name: --expand-tabs
tip: Perform a tab expansion (replace each tab with enough spaces to fill to the next display column that is a multiple of <n>) in the log message before showing it in the output. --expand-tabs is a short-hand for --expand-tabs=8, and --no-expand-tabs is a short-hand for --expand-tabs=0, which disables tab expansion.

option.name: --ext-diff
tip: Allow an external diff helper to be executed.
If you set an external diff driver with gitattributes(5), you need to use this option with git-log(1) and friends.

option.name: --extended-regexp
tip: Consider the limiting patterns to be extended regular expressions instead of the default basic regular expressions.

option.name: --find-copies
tip: Detect copies as well as renames.
See also --find-copies-harder.
If <n> is specified, it has the same meaning as for -M<n>.

option.name: --find-copies-harder
tip: For performance reasons, by default, -C option finds copies only if the original file of the copy was modified in the same changeset.
This flag makes the command inspect unmodified files as candidates for the source of copy.
This is a very expensive operation for large projects, so use it with caution.
Giving more than one -C option has the same effect.

option.name: --find-object
tip: Look for differences that change the number of occurrences of the specified object.
Similar to -S, just the argument is different in that it doesn't search for a specific string but for a specific object id.

option.name: --find-renames
tip: If generating diffs, detect and report renames for each commit.
For following files across renames while traversing history, see --follow.
If <n> is specified, it is a threshold on the similarity index (i.e. amount of addition/deletions compared to the file's size).
For example, -M90% means Git should consider a delete/add pair to be a rename if more than 90% of the file hasn't changed.

option.name: --first-parent
tip: When finding commits to include, follow only the first parent commit upon seeing a merge commit.

This option can give a better overview when viewing the evolution of a particular topic branch, because merges into a topic branch tend to be only about adjusting to updated upstream from time to time, and this option allows you to ignore the individual commits brought in to your history by such a merge.

option.name: --fixed-strings
tip: Consider the limiting patterns to be fixed strings (don't interpret pattern as a regular expression).

option.name: --follow
tip: Continue listing the history of a file beyond renames (works only for a single file).

option.name: --format
tip: Pretty-print the contents of the commit logs in a given format, where <format> can be one of oneline, short, medium, full, fuller, reference, email, raw, format:<string> and tformat:<string>.
When <format> is none of the above, and has %<placeholder> in it, it acts as if --pretty=tformat:<format> were given.

option.name: --full-diff
tip: Without this flag, git log -p <path>... shows commits that touch the specified paths, and diffs about the same specified paths.
With this, the full diff is shown for commits that touch the specified paths; this means that "<path>..." limits only commits, and doesn't limit diff for those commits.

option.name: --full-history
tip: Same as the default mode, but does not prune some history.

option.name: --full-index
tip: Instead of the first handful of characters, show the full pre- and post-image blob object names on the "index" line when generating patch format output.

option.name: --function-context
tip: Show whole function as context lines for each change.
The function names are determined in the same way as git diff works out patch hunk headers (see "Defining a custom hunk-header" in gitattributes(5)).

option.name: --glob
tip: Pretend as if all the refs matching shell glob <glob-pattern> are listed on the command line as <commit>.
Leading refs/, is automatically prepended if missing.
If pattern lacks ?, *, or [, /* at the end is implied.

option.name: --graph
tip: Draw a text-based graphical representation of the commit history on the left hand side of the output.
This may cause extra lines to be printed in between commits, in order for the graph history to be drawn properly.
Cannot be combined with --no-walk.

option.name: --graph-indent
tip: When used with --graph, indent visual roots (commits with no parents or whose parents are not shown) to differentiate them from commits that are vertically adjacent but unrelated.
Enabled by default.
Use --no-graph-indent to disable or set log.graphIndent to set a default preference.

option.name: --graph-lane-limit
tip: When --graph is used, limit the number of graph lanes to be shown.
Lanes over the limit are replaced with a truncation mark ~.
By default it is set to 0 (no limit), zero and negative values are ignored and treated as no limit.

option.name: --grep
tip: Limit the commits output to ones with a log message that matches the <pattern> regular expression.
With more than one --grep=<pattern>, commits whose message matches any of the <pattern> are chosen (but see --all-match).

option.name: --grep-reflog
tip: Limit the commits output to ones with reflog entries that match the <pattern> regular expression.
With more than one --grep-reflog, commits whose reflog message matches any of the given patterns are chosen.
It is an error to use this option unless --walk-reflogs is in use.

option.name: --histogram
tip: Generate a diff using the "histogram diff" algorithm.

option.name: --ignore-all-space
tip: Ignore whitespace when comparing lines.
This ignores differences even if one line has whitespace where the other line has none.

option.name: --ignore-blank-lines
tip: Ignore changes whose lines are all blank.

option.name: --ignore-cr-at-eol
tip: Ignore carriage-return at the end of line when doing a comparison.

option.name: --ignore-matching-lines
tip: Ignore changes whose all lines match <regex>.
This option may be specified more than once.

option.name: --ignore-missing
tip: Upon seeing an invalid object name in the input, pretend as if the bad input was not given.

option.name: --ignore-space-at-eol
tip: Ignore changes in whitespace at EOL.

option.name: --ignore-space-change
tip: Ignore changes in amount of whitespace.
This ignores whitespace at line end, and considers all other sequences of one or more whitespace characters to be equivalent.

option.name: --ignore-submodules
tip: Ignore changes to submodules in the diff generation. all is the default.

Using none will consider the submodule modified when it either contains untracked or modified files or its HEAD differs from the commit recorded in the superproject and can be used to override any settings of the ignore option in git-config(1) or gitmodules(5).
When untracked is used submodules are not considered dirty when they only contain untracked content (but they are still scanned for modified content).
Using dirty ignores all changes to the work tree of submodules, only changes to the commits stored in the superproject are shown (this was the behavior until 1.7.0).

option.name: --indent-heuristic
tip: Enable the heuristic that shifts diff hunk boundaries to make patches easier to read.
This is the default.

option.name: --inter-hunk-context
tip: Show the context between diff hunks, up to the specified <number> of lines, thereby fusing hunks that are close to each other.
Defaults to diff.interHunkContext or 0 if the config option is unset.

option.name: --invert-grep
tip: Limit the commits output to ones with a log message that do not match the <pattern> specified with --grep=<pattern>.

option.name: --irreversible-delete
tip: Omit the preimage for deletes, i.e. print only the header but not the diff between the preimage and /dev/null.
The resulting patch is not meant to be applied with patch or git apply; this is solely for people who want to just concentrate on reviewing the text after the change.
In addition, the output obviously lacks enough information to apply such a patch in reverse, even manually, hence the name of the option.

option.name: --ita-invisible-in-index
tip: By default entries added by git add -N appear as an existing empty file in git diff and a new file in git diff --cached.
This option makes the entry appear as a new file in git diff and non-existent in git diff --cached.
This option could be reverted with --ita-visible-in-index.
Both options are experimental and could be removed in future.

option.name: --left-only
tip: List only commits on the respective side of a symmetric difference, i.e. only those which would be marked < resp. > by --left-right.

option.name: --left-right
tip: Mark which side of a symmetric difference a commit is reachable from.
Commits from the left side are prefixed with < and those from the right with >.
If combined with --boundary, those commits are prefixed with -.

option.name: --line-prefix
tip: Prepend an additional <prefix> to every line of output.

option.name: --log-size
tip: Include a line log size <number> in the output for each commit, where <number> is the length of that commit's message in bytes.
Intended to speed up tools that read log messages from git log output by allowing them to allocate space in advance.

option.name: --mailmap
tip: Use mailmap file to map author and committer names and email addresses to canonical real names and email addresses.
See git-shortlog(1).

option.name: --max-count
tip: Limit the output to the first <number> commits that would be shown.

option.name: --max-count-oldest
tip: Limit the output to the last <number> commits that would be shown.

option.name: --max-depth
tip: For each pathspec given on command line, descend at most <depth> levels of directories.
A value of -1 means no limit.
Cannot be combined with wildcards in the pathspec.
Given a tree containing foo/bar/baz, the following list shows the matches generated by each set of options:

option.name: --max-parents
tip: Show only commits which have at least (or at most) that many parent commits.
In particular, --max-parents=1 is the same as --no-merges, --min-parents=2 is the same as --merges. --max-parents=0 gives all root commits and --min-parents=3 all octopus merges.

option.name: --maximal-only
tip: Restrict the output commits to be those that are not reachable from any other commits in the revision range.

option.name: --merge
tip: Show commits touching conflicted paths in the range HEAD...<other>, where <other> is the first existing pseudoref in MERGE_HEAD, CHERRY_PICK_HEAD, REVERT_HEAD or REBASE_HEAD.
Only works when the index has unmerged entries.
This option can be used to show relevant commits when resolving conflicts from a 3-way merge.

option.name: --merges
tip: Print only merge commits.
This is exactly the same as --min-parents=2.

option.name: --min-parents
tip: Show only commits which have at least (or at most) that many parent commits.
In particular, --max-parents=1 is the same as --no-merges, --min-parents=2 is the same as --merges. --max-parents=0 gives all root commits and --min-parents=3 all octopus merges.

option.name: --minimal
tip: Spend extra time to make sure the smallest possible diff is produced.

option.name: --name-only
tip: Show only the name of each changed file in the post-image tree.
The file names are often encoded in UTF-8.
For more information see the discussion about encoding in the git-log(1) manual page.

option.name: --name-status
tip: Show only the name(s) and status of each changed file.
See the description of the --diff-filter option on what the status letters mean.
Just like --name-only the file names are often encoded in UTF-8.

option.name: --no-abbrev-commit
tip: Show the full 40-byte hexadecimal commit object name.
This negates --abbrev-commit, either explicit or implied by other options such as --oneline.
It also overrides the log.abbrevCommit variable.

option.name: --no-all
tip: Disable --all.

option.name: --no-all-match
tip: Disable --all-match.

option.name: --no-alternate-refs
tip: Disable --alternate-refs.

option.name: --no-author-date-order
tip: Disable --author-date-order.

option.name: --no-basic-regexp
tip: Disable --basic-regexp.

option.name: --no-binary
tip: Disable --binary.

option.name: --no-bisect
tip: Disable --bisect.

option.name: --no-boundary
tip: Disable --boundary.

option.name: --no-cc
tip: Disable --cc.

option.name: --no-check
tip: Disable --check.

option.name: --no-cherry
tip: Disable --cherry.

option.name: --no-cherry-mark
tip: Disable --cherry-mark.

option.name: --no-cherry-pick
tip: Disable --cherry-pick.

option.name: --no-children
tip: Disable --children.

option.name: --no-clear-decorations
tip: Disable --clear-decorations.

option.name: --no-color
tip: Turn off colored diff.
It is the same as --color=never.

option.name: --no-color-moved
tip: Turn off move detection.
This can be used to override configuration settings.
It is the same as --color-moved=no.

option.name: --no-color-moved-ws
tip: Do not ignore whitespace when performing move detection.
This can be used to override configuration settings.
It is the same as --color-moved-ws=no.

option.name: --no-combined-all-paths
tip: Disable --combined-all-paths.

option.name: --no-compact-summary
tip: Disable --compact-summary.

option.name: --no-cumulative
tip: Disable --cumulative.

option.name: --no-date-order
tip: Disable --date-order.

option.name: --no-dd
tip: Disable --dd.

option.name: --no-decorate
tip: Print out the ref names of any commits that are shown.
Possible values are:

option.name: --no-default-prefix
tip: Disable --default-prefix.

option.name: --no-dense
tip: Disable --dense.

option.name: --no-diff-merges
tip: Synonym for --diff-merges=off.

option.name: --no-do-walk
tip: Disable --do-walk.

option.name: --no-exclude-first-parent-only
tip: Disable --exclude-first-parent-only.

option.name: --no-exit-code
tip: Disable --exit-code.

option.name: --no-expand-tabs
tip: Perform a tab expansion (replace each tab with enough spaces to fill to the next display column that is a multiple of <n>) in the log message before showing it in the output. --expand-tabs is a short-hand for --expand-tabs=8, and --no-expand-tabs is a short-hand for --expand-tabs=0, which disables tab expansion.

option.name: --no-ext-diff
tip: Disallow external diff drivers.

option.name: --no-extended-regexp
tip: Disable --extended-regexp.

option.name: --no-find-copies-harder
tip: Disable --find-copies-harder.

option.name: --no-first-parent
tip: Disable --first-parent.

option.name: --no-fixed-strings
tip: Disable --fixed-strings.

option.name: --no-follow
tip: Disable --follow.

option.name: --no-full-diff
tip: Disable --full-diff.

option.name: --no-full-index
tip: Disable --full-index.

option.name: --no-function-context
tip: Disable --function-context.

option.name: --no-graph
tip: Disable --graph.

option.name: --no-graph-indent
tip: When used with --graph, indent visual roots (commits with no parents or whose parents are not shown) to differentiate them from commits that are vertically adjacent but unrelated.
Enabled by default.
Use --no-graph-indent to disable or set log.graphIndent to set a default preference.

option.name: --no-histogram
tip: Disable --histogram.

option.name: --no-ignore-all-space
tip: Disable --ignore-all-space.

option.name: --no-ignore-blank-lines
tip: Disable --ignore-blank-lines.

option.name: --no-ignore-cr-at-eol
tip: Disable --ignore-cr-at-eol.

option.name: --no-ignore-missing
tip: Disable --ignore-missing.

option.name: --no-ignore-space-at-eol
tip: Disable --ignore-space-at-eol.

option.name: --no-ignore-space-change
tip: Disable --ignore-space-change.

option.name: --no-indent-heuristic
tip: Disable the indent heuristic.

option.name: --no-invert-grep
tip: Disable --invert-grep.

option.name: --no-irreversible-delete
tip: Disable --irreversible-delete.

option.name: --no-ita-invisible-in-index
tip: Disable --ita-invisible-in-index.

option.name: --no-left-only
tip: Disable --left-only.

option.name: --no-left-right
tip: Disable --left-right.

option.name: --no-log-size
tip: Disable --log-size.

option.name: --no-mailmap
tip: Use mailmap file to map author and committer names and email addresses to canonical real names and email addresses.
See git-shortlog(1).

option.name: --no-max-parents
tip: Show only commits which have at least (or at most) that many parent commits.
In particular, --max-parents=1 is the same as --no-merges, --min-parents=2 is the same as --merges. --max-parents=0 gives all root commits and --min-parents=3 all octopus merges.

option.name: --no-maximal-only
tip: Disable --maximal-only.

option.name: --no-merge
tip: Disable --merge.

option.name: --no-merges
tip: Do not print commits with more than one parent.
This is exactly the same as --max-parents=1.

option.name: --no-min-parents
tip: Show only commits which have at least (or at most) that many parent commits.
In particular, --max-parents=1 is the same as --no-merges, --min-parents=2 is the same as --merges. --max-parents=0 gives all root commits and --min-parents=3 all octopus merges.

option.name: --no-minimal
tip: Disable --minimal.

option.name: --no-name-only
tip: Disable --name-only.

option.name: --no-name-status
tip: Disable --name-status.

option.name: --no-not
tip: Disable --not.

option.name: --no-notes
tip: Do not show notes.
This negates the above --notes option, by resetting the list of notes refs from which notes are shown.
Options are parsed in the order given on the command line, so e.g. "--notes --notes=foo --no-notes --notes=bar" will only show notes from refs/notes/bar.

option.name: --no-numstat
tip: Disable --numstat.

option.name: --no-oneline
tip: Disable --oneline.

option.name: --no-parents
tip: Disable --parents.

option.name: --no-patch
tip: Suppress all output from the diff machinery.
Useful for commands like git show that show the patch by default to squelch their output, or to cancel the effect of options like --patch, --stat earlier on the command line in an alias.

option.name: --no-patch-with-raw
tip: Disable --patch-with-raw.

option.name: --no-patch-with-stat
tip: Disable --patch-with-stat.

option.name: --no-patience
tip: Disable --patience.

option.name: --no-perl-regexp
tip: Disable --perl-regexp.

option.name: --no-pickaxe-all
tip: Disable --pickaxe-all.

option.name: --no-pickaxe-regex
tip: Disable --pickaxe-regex.

option.name: --no-prefix
tip: Do not show any source or destination prefix.

option.name: --no-raw
tip: Disable --raw.

option.name: --no-reflog
tip: Disable --reflog.

option.name: --no-regexp-ignore-case
tip: Disable --regexp-ignore-case.

option.name: --no-relative
tip: When run from a subdirectory of the project, it can be told to exclude changes outside the directory and show pathnames relative to it with this option.

When you are not in a subdirectory (e.g. in a bare repository), you can name which subdirectory to make the output relative to by giving a <path> as an argument. --no-relative can be used to countermand both diff.relative config option and previous --relative.

option.name: --no-relative-date
tip: Disable --relative-date.

option.name: --no-remerge-diff
tip: Disable --remerge-diff.

option.name: --no-remove-empty
tip: Disable --remove-empty.

option.name: --no-rename-empty
tip: Whether to use empty blobs as rename source.

option.name: --no-renames
tip: Turn off rename detection, even when the configuration file gives the default to do so.

option.name: --no-reverse
tip: Disable --reverse.

option.name: --no-right-only
tip: Disable --right-only.

option.name: --no-shortstat
tip: Disable --shortstat.

option.name: --no-show-notes-by-default
tip: Disable --show-notes-by-default.

option.name: --no-show-pulls
tip: Disable --show-pulls.

option.name: --no-show-signature
tip: Disable --show-signature.

option.name: --no-simplify-by-decoration
tip: Disable --simplify-by-decoration.

option.name: --no-simplify-merges
tip: Disable --simplify-merges.

option.name: --no-single-worktree
tip: Disable --single-worktree.

option.name: --no-source
tip: Disable --source.

option.name: --no-sparse
tip: Disable --sparse.

option.name: --no-standard-notes
tip: These options are deprecated.
Use the above --notes/--no-notes options instead.

option.name: --no-stdin
tip: Disable --stdin.

option.name: --no-summary
tip: Disable --summary.

option.name: --no-text
tip: Disable --text.

option.name: --no-textconv
tip: Allow (or disallow) external text conversion filters to be run when comparing binary files.
See gitattributes(5) for details.
Because textconv filters are typically a one-way conversion, the resulting diff is suitable for human consumption, but cannot be applied.
For this reason, textconv filters are enabled by default only for git-diff(1) and git-log(1), but not for git-format-patch(1) or diff plumbing commands.

option.name: --no-topo-order
tip: Disable --topo-order.

option.name: --no-use-mailmap
tip: Use mailmap file to map author and committer names and email addresses to canonical real names and email addresses.
See git-shortlog(1).

option.name: --no-walk
tip: Only show the given commits, but do not traverse their ancestors.
This has no effect if a range is specified.
If the argument unsorted is given, the commits are shown in the order they were given on the command line.
Otherwise (if sorted or no argument was given), the commits are shown in reverse chronological order by commit time.

option.name: --no-walk-reflogs
tip: Disable --walk-reflogs.

option.name: --not
tip: Reverses the meaning of the ^ prefix (or lack thereof) for all following revision specifiers, up to the next --not.
When used on the command line before --stdin, the revisions passed through stdin will not be affected by it.
Conversely, when passed via standard input, the revisions passed on the command line will not be affected by it.

option.name: --notes
tip: Show the notes (see git-notes(1)) that annotate the commit, when showing the commit log message.
This is the default for git log, git show and git whatchanged commands when there is no --pretty, --format, or --oneline option given on the command line.

option.name: --numstat
tip: Similar to --stat, but shows number of added and deleted lines in decimal notation and pathname without abbreviation, to make it more machine friendly.
For binary files, outputs two - instead of saying 0 0.

option.name: --oneline
tip: This is a shorthand for --pretty=oneline --abbrev-commit used together.

option.name: --output
tip: Output to a specific file instead of stdout.

option.name: --output-indicator-context
tip: Specify the character used to indicate new, old or context lines in the generated patch.
Normally they are +, - and ' ' respectively.

option.name: --output-indicator-new
tip: Specify the character used to indicate new, old or context lines in the generated patch.
Normally they are +, - and ' ' respectively.

option.name: --output-indicator-old
tip: Specify the character used to indicate new, old or context lines in the generated patch.
Normally they are +, - and ' ' respectively.

option.name: --parents
tip: Print also the parents of the commit (in the form "commit parent...:").
Also enables parent rewriting, see History Simplification above.

option.name: --patch
tip: Generate patch (see the section called "GENERATING PATCH TEXT WITH -P").

option.name: --patch-with-raw
tip: Synonym for -p --raw.

option.name: --patch-with-stat
tip: Synonym for -p --stat.

option.name: --patience
tip: Generate a diff using the "patience diff" algorithm.

option.name: --perl-regexp
tip: Consider the limiting patterns to be Perl-compatible regular expressions.

option.name: --pickaxe-all
tip: When -S or -G finds a change, show all the changes in that changeset, not just the files that contain the change in <string>.

option.name: --pickaxe-regex
tip: Treat the <string> given to -S as an extended POSIX regular expression to match.

option.name: --pretty
tip: Pretty-print the contents of the commit logs in a given format, where <format> can be one of oneline, short, medium, full, fuller, reference, email, raw, format:<string> and tformat:<string>.
When <format> is none of the above, and has %<placeholder> in it, it acts as if --pretty=tformat:<format> were given.

next.name: format:<string>
tip: Control the format of displayed information.

next.name: full
tip: Display hash, Author, Commit, and commit info.

next.name: fuller
tip: Display hash, Author, AuthorDate, Commit, CommitDate, and commit info.

next.name: oneline
tip: Display each commit message on one line, showing only the hash and commit message.

next.name: short
tip: Display hash, Author, and commit info.

option.name: --raw
tip: For each commit, show a summary of changes using the raw diff format.
See the "RAW OUTPUT FORMAT" section of git-diff(1).
This is different from showing the log itself in raw format, which you can achieve with --format=raw.

option.name: --reflog
tip: Pretend as if all objects mentioned by reflogs are listed on the command line as <commit>.

option.name: --regexp-ignore-case
tip: Match the regular expression limiting patterns without regard to letter case.

option.name: --relative
tip: When run from a subdirectory of the project, it can be told to exclude changes outside the directory and show pathnames relative to it with this option.

When you are not in a subdirectory (e.g. in a bare repository), you can name which subdirectory to make the output relative to by giving a <path> as an argument. --no-relative can be used to countermand both diff.relative config option and previous --relative.

option.name: --relative-date
tip: Synonym for --date=relative.

option.name: --remerge-diff
tip: Produce remerge-diff output for merge commits.
Shortcut for --diff-merges=remerge -p.

option.name: --remotes
tip: Pretend as if all the refs in refs/remotes are listed on the command line as <commit>.
If <pattern> is given, limit remote-tracking branches to ones matching given shell glob.
If pattern lacks ?, *, or [, /* at the end is implied.

option.name: --remove-empty
tip: Stop when a given path disappears from the tree.

option.name: --rename-empty
tip: Whether to use empty blobs as rename source.

option.name: --reverse
tip: Output the commits chosen to be shown (see Commit Limiting section above) in reverse order.
Cannot be combined with --walk-reflogs.

option.name: --right-only
tip: List only commits on the respective side of a symmetric difference, i.e. only those which would be marked < resp. > by --left-right.

option.name: --rotate-to
tip: Discard the files before the named <file> from the output (i.e. skip to), or move them to the end of the output (i.e. rotate to).
These options were invented primarily for the use of the git difftool command, and may not be very useful otherwise.

option.name: --shortstat
tip: Output only the last line of the --stat format containing total number of modified files, as well as number of added and deleted lines.

option.name: --show-linear-break
tip: When --graph is not used, all history branches are flattened which can make it hard to see that the two consecutive commits do not belong to a linear branch.
This option puts a barrier in between them in that case.
If <barrier> is specified, it is the string that will be shown instead of the default one.

option.name: --show-notes
tip: These options are deprecated.
Use the above --notes/--no-notes options instead.

option.name: --show-notes-by-default
tip: Show the default notes unless options for displaying specific notes are given.

option.name: --show-pulls
tip: Include all commits from the default mode, but also any merge commits that are not TREESAME to the first parent but are TREESAME to a later parent.
This mode is helpful for showing the merge commits that "first introduced" a change to a branch.

option.name: --show-signature
tip: Check the validity of a signed commit object by passing the signature to gpg --verify and show the output.

option.name: --simplify-by-decoration
tip: Commits that are referred by some branch or tag are selected.

option.name: --simplify-merges
tip: Additional option to --full-history to remove some needless merges from the resulting history, as there are no selected commits contributing to this merge.

option.name: --since
tip: Show commits more recent than <date>.
As a special case, today means the last midnight.

option.name: --since-as-filter
tip: Show all commits more recent than <date>.
This visits all commits in the range, rather than stopping at the first commit which is older than <date>.

option.name: --single-worktree
tip: By default, all working trees will be examined by the following options when there are more than one (see git-worktree(1)): --all, --reflog and --indexed-objects.
This option forces them to examine the current working tree only.

option.name: --skip
tip: Skip <number> commits before starting to show the commit output.

option.name: --skip-to
tip: Discard the files before the named <file> from the output (i.e. skip to), or move them to the end of the output (i.e. rotate to).
These options were invented primarily for the use of the git difftool command, and may not be very useful otherwise.

option.name: --source
tip: Print out the ref name given on the command line by which each commit was reached.

option.name: --sparse
tip: All commits in the simplified history are shown.

option.name: --src-prefix
tip: Show the given source <prefix> instead of "a/".

option.name: --standard-notes
tip: These options are deprecated.
Use the above --notes/--no-notes options instead.

option.name: --stat
tip: Generate a diffstat.
By default, as much space as necessary will be used for the filename part, and the rest for the graph part.
Maximum width defaults to terminal width, or 80 columns if not connected to a terminal, and can be overridden by <width>.
The width of the filename part can be limited by giving another width <name-width> after a comma or by setting diff.statNameWidth=<name-width>.

option.name: --stdin
tip: In addition to getting arguments from the command line, read them from standard input as well.
This accepts commits and pseudo-options like --all and --glob=.
When a -- separator is seen, the following input is treated as paths and used to limit the result.
Flags like --not which are read via standard input are only respected for arguments passed in the same way and will not influence any subsequent command line arguments.

option.name: --submodule
tip: Specify how differences in submodules are shown.
When specifying --submodule=short the short format is used.
This format just shows the names of the commits at the beginning and end of the range.
When --submodule or --submodule=log is specified, the log format is used.

option.name: --summary
tip: Output a condensed summary of extended header information such as creations, renames and mode changes.

option.name: --tags
tip: Pretend as if all the refs in refs/tags are listed on the command line as <commit>.
If <pattern> is given, limit tags to ones matching given shell glob.
If pattern lacks ?, *, or [, /* at the end is implied.

option.name: --text
tip: Treat all files as text.

option.name: --textconv
tip: Allow (or disallow) external text conversion filters to be run when comparing binary files.
See gitattributes(5) for details.
Because textconv filters are typically a one-way conversion, the resulting diff is suitable for human consumption, but cannot be applied.
For this reason, textconv filters are enabled by default only for git-diff(1) and git-log(1), but not for git-format-patch(1) or diff plumbing commands.

option.name: --topo-order
tip: Show no parents before all of its children are shown, and avoid showing commits on multiple lines of history intermixed.

option.name: --unified
tip: Generate diffs with <n> lines of context.
The number of context lines defaults to diff.context or 3 if the configuration variable is unset.
(-U without <n> is silently accepted as a synonym for -p due to a historical accident).
Implies --patch.

option.name: --until
tip: Show commits older than <date>.

option.name: --use-mailmap
tip: Use mailmap file to map author and committer names and email addresses to canonical real names and email addresses.
See git-shortlog(1).

option.name: --walk-reflogs
tip: Instead of walking the commit ancestry chain, walk reflog entries from the most recent one to older ones.
When this option is used you cannot specify commits to exclude (that is, ^<commit>, <commit1>..<commit2>, and <commit1>...<commit2> notations cannot be used).

option.name: --word-diff
tip: By default, words are delimited by whitespace; see --word-diff-regex below.
The <mode> defaults to plain, and must be one of:

option.name: --word-diff-regex
tip: Use <regex> to decide what a word is, instead of considering runs of non-whitespace to be a word.
Also implies --word-diff unless it was already enabled.

option.name: --ws-error-highlight
tip: Highlight whitespace errors in the context, old or new lines of the diff.
Multiple values are separated by comma, none resets previous values, default reset the list to new and all is a shorthand for old,new,context.
When this option is not given, and the configuration variable diff.wsErrorHighlight is not set, only whitespace errors in new lines are highlighted.
The whitespace errors are colored with color.diff.whitespace.

option.name: -c
tip: Produce combined diff output for merge commits.
Shortcut for --diff-merges=combined -p.

option.name: -G
tip: Look for differences whose patch text contains added/removed lines that match <regex>.

option.name: -l
tip: The -M and -C options involve some preliminary steps that can detect subsets of renames/copies cheaply, followed by an exhaustive fallback portion that compares all remaining unpaired destinations to all relevant sources.
(For renames, only remaining unpaired sources are relevant; for copies, all original sources are relevant.) For N sources and destinations, this exhaustive check is O(N^2).
This option prevents the exhaustive portion of rename/copy detection from running if the number of source/destination files involved exceeds the specified number.
Defaults to diff.renameLimit.

option.name: -L
tip: Trace the evolution of the line range given by <start>,<end>, or by the function name regex <funcname>, within the <file>.
You may not give any pathspec limiters.

This is currently limited to a walk starting from a single revision, i.e., you may only give zero or one positive revision arguments, and <start> and <end> (or <funcname>) must exist in the starting revision.
You can specify this option more than once.

option.name: -m
tip: Show diffs for merge commits in the default format.
This is similar to --diff-merges=on, except -m will produce no output unless -p is given as well.

option.name: -O
tip: Control the order in which files appear in the output.
This overrides the diff.orderFile configuration variable (see git-config(1)).
To cancel diff.orderFile, use -O/dev/null.

option.name: -R
tip: Swap two inputs; that is, show differences from index or on-disk file to tree contents.

option.name: -S
tip: Look for differences that change the number of occurrences of the specified <string> (i.e. addition/deletion) in a file.
Intended for the scripter's use.

option.name: -t
tip: Show the tree objects in the diff output.

option.name: -z
tip: Separate the commits with NULs instead of newlines.

next.name: ls-files
tip: Show information about files in the index and working directory.

option.name: --abbrev
tip: Instead of showing the full 40-byte hexadecimal object lines, show the shortest prefix that is at least <n> hexdigits long that uniquely refers the object.
Non default number of digits can be specified with --abbrev=<n>.

option.name: --cached
tip: Show all files cached in Git's index, i.e. all tracked files.
(This is the default if no -c/-s/-d/-o/-u/-k/-m/--resolve-undo options are specified.)

option.name: --debug
tip: After each line that describes a file, add more data about its cache entry.
This is intended to show as much information as possible for manual inspection; the exact format may change at any time.

option.name: --deduplicate
tip: When only filenames are shown, suppress duplicates that may come from having multiple stages during a merge, or giving --deleted and --modified option at the same time.
When any of the -t, --unmerged, or --stage option is in use, this option has no effect.

option.name: --deleted
tip: Show files with an unstaged deletion

option.name: --directory
tip: If a whole directory is classified as "other", show just its name (with a trailing slash) and not its whole contents.
Has no effect without -o/--others.

option.name: --eol
tip: Show <eolinfo> and <eolattr> of files. <eolinfo> is the file content identification used by Git when the "text" attribute is "auto" (or not set and core.autocrlf is not false). <eolinfo> is either "-text", "none", "lf", "crlf", "mixed" or "".

option.name: --error-unmatch
tip: If any <file> does not appear in the index, treat this as an error (return 1).

option.name: --exclude
tip: Skip untracked files matching pattern.
Note that pattern is a shell wildcard pattern.
See EXCLUDE PATTERNS below for more information.

option.name: --exclude-from
tip: Read exclude patterns from <file>; 1 per line.

option.name: --exclude-per-directory
tip: Read additional exclude patterns that apply only to the directory and its subdirectories in <file>.
If you are trying to emulate the way Porcelain commands work, using the --exclude-standard option instead is easier and more thorough.

option.name: --exclude-standard
tip: Add the standard Git exclusions: .git/info/exclude, .gitignore in each directory, and the user's global exclusion file.

option.name: --format
tip: A string that interpolates %(fieldname) from the result being shown.

It also interpolates %% to %, and %xXX where XX are hex digits interpolates to character with hex code XX; for example %x00 interpolates to \0 (NUL), %x09 to \t (TAB) and %x0a to \n (LF). --format cannot be combined with -s, -o, -k, -t, --resolve-undo and --eol.

option.name: --full-name
tip: When run from a subdirectory, the command usually outputs paths relative to the current directory.
This option forces paths to be output relative to the project top directory.

option.name: --ignored
tip: Show only ignored files in the output.
Must be used with either an explicit -c or -o.
When showing files in the index (i.e. when used with -c), print only those files matching an exclude pattern.
When showing "other" files (i.e. when used with -o), show only those matched by an exclude pattern.

option.name: --killed
tip: Show untracked files on the filesystem that need to be removed due to file/directory conflicts for tracked files to be able to be written to the filesystem.

option.name: --modified
tip: Show files with an unstaged modification (note that an unstaged deletion also counts as an unstaged modification)

option.name: --no-cached
tip: Disable --cached.

option.name: --no-debug
tip: Disable --debug.

option.name: --no-deduplicate
tip: Disable --deduplicate.

option.name: --no-deleted
tip: Disable --deleted.

option.name: --no-directory
tip: Disable --directory.

option.name: --no-empty-directory
tip: Do not list empty directories.
Has no effect without --directory.

option.name: --no-eol
tip: Disable --eol.

option.name: --no-error-unmatch
tip: Disable --error-unmatch.

option.name: --no-ignored
tip: Disable --ignored.

option.name: --no-killed
tip: Disable --killed.

option.name: --no-modified
tip: Disable --modified.

option.name: --no-others
tip: Disable --others.

option.name: --no-recurse-submodules
tip: Disable --recurse-submodules.

option.name: --no-resolve-undo
tip: Disable --resolve-undo.

option.name: --no-sparse
tip: Disable --sparse.

option.name: --no-stage
tip: Disable --stage.

option.name: --no-unmerged
tip: Disable --unmerged.

option.name: --others
tip: Show other (i.e. untracked) files in the output

option.name: --recurse-submodules
tip: Recursively calls ls-files on each active submodule in the repository.
Currently there is only support for the --cached and --stage modes.

option.name: --resolve-undo
tip: Show files having resolve-undo information in the index together with their resolve-undo information.
(resolve-undo information is what is used to implement "git checkout -m $PATH", i.e. to recreate merge conflicts that were accidentally resolved)

option.name: --sparse
tip: If the index is sparse, show the sparse directories without expanding to the contained files.
Sparse directories will be shown with a trailing slash, such as "x/" for a sparse directory "x".

option.name: --stage
tip: Show staged contents' mode bits, object name and stage number in the output.

option.name: --unmerged
tip: Show information about unmerged files in the output, but do not show any other tracked files (forces --stage, overrides --cached).

option.name: --with-tree
tip: When using --error-unmatch to expand the user supplied <file> (i.e. path pattern) arguments to paths, pretend that paths which were removed in the index since the named <tree-ish> are still present.
Using this option with -s or -u options does not make any sense.

option.name: -f
tip: Similar to -t, but use lowercase letters for files that are marked as fsmonitor valid (see git-update-index(1)).

option.name: -t
tip: Show status tags together with filenames.

Note that for scripting purposes, git-status(1) --porcelain and git-diff-files(1) --name-status are almost always superior alternatives; users should look at git-status(1) --short or git-diff(1) --name-status for more user-friendly alternatives.

option.name: -v
tip: Similar to -t, but use lowercase letters for files that are marked as assume unchanged (see git-update-index(1)).

option.name: -z
tip: \0 line termination on output and do not quote filenames.
See OUTPUT below for more information.

next.name: ls-remote
tip: List references in a remote repository.

option.name: --branches
tip: Limit to only local branches and local tags, respectively.
These options are not mutually exclusive; when given both, references stored in refs/heads and refs/tags are displayed.
Note that --heads and -h are deprecated synonyms for --branches and -b and may be removed in the future.
Also note that git ls-remote -h used without anything else on the command line gives help, consistent with other git subcommands.

option.name: --exit-code
tip: Exit with status "2" when no matching refs are found in the remote repository.
Usually the command exits with status "0" to indicate it successfully talked with the remote repository, whether it found any matching refs.

option.name: --get-url
tip: Expand the URL of the given remote repository taking into account any "url.<base>.insteadOf" config setting (See git-config(1)) and exit without talking to the remote.

option.name: --no-branches
tip: Disable --branches.

option.name: --no-exit-code
tip: Disable --exit-code.

option.name: --no-get-url
tip: Disable --get-url.

option.name: --no-quiet
tip: Disable --quiet.

option.name: --no-refs
tip: Disable --refs.

option.name: --no-symref
tip: Disable --symref.

option.name: --no-tags
tip: Disable --tags.

option.name: --quiet
tip: Do not print remote URL to stderr.

option.name: --refs
tip: Do not show peeled tags or pseudorefs like HEAD in the output.

option.name: --server-option
tip: Transmit the given string to the server when communicating using protocol version 2.
The given string must not contain a NUL or LF character.
When multiple --server-option=<option> are given, they are all sent to the other side in the order listed on the command line.
When no --server-option=<option> is given from the command line, the values of configuration variable remote.<name>.serverOption are used instead.

option.name: --sort
tip: Sort based on the key given.
Prefix - to sort in descending order of the value.
Supports "version:refname" or "v:refname" (tag names are treated as versions).
The "version:refname" sort order can also be affected by the "versionsort.suffix" configuration variable.

option.name: --symref
tip: In addition to the object pointed by it, show the underlying ref pointed by it when showing a symbolic ref.
Currently, upload-pack only shows the symref HEAD, so it will be the only one shown by ls-remote.

option.name: --tags
tip: Limit to only local branches and local tags, respectively.
These options are not mutually exclusive; when given both, references stored in refs/heads and refs/tags are displayed.
Note that --heads and -h are deprecated synonyms for --branches and -b and may be removed in the future.
Also note that git ls-remote -h used without anything else on the command line gives help, consistent with other git subcommands.

option.name: --upload-pack
tip: Specify the full path of git-upload-pack on the remote host.
This allows listing references from repositories accessed via SSH and where the SSH daemon does not use the PATH configured by the user.

next.name: ls-tree
tip: List the contents of a tree object.

option.name: --abbrev
tip: Instead of showing the full 40-byte hexadecimal object lines, show the shortest prefix that is at least <n> hexdigits long that uniquely refers the object.
Non default number of digits can be specified with --abbrev=<n>.

option.name: --format
tip: A string that interpolates %(fieldname) from the result being shown.
It also interpolates %% to %, and %xNN where NN are hex digits interpolates to character with hex code NN; for example %x00 interpolates to \0 (NUL), %x09 to \t (TAB) and %x0a to \n (LF).
When specified, --format cannot be combined with other format-altering options, including --long, --name-only and --object-only.

option.name: --full-name
tip: Instead of showing the path names relative to the current working directory, show the full path names.

option.name: --full-tree
tip: Do not limit the listing to the current working directory.
Implies --full-name.

option.name: --long
tip: Show object size of blob (file) entries.

option.name: --name-only
tip: List only filenames (instead of the "long" output), one per line.
Cannot be combined with --object-only.

option.name: --name-status
tip: List only filenames (instead of the "long" output), one per line.
Cannot be combined with --object-only.

option.name: --no-full-name
tip: Disable --full-name.

option.name: --no-full-tree
tip: Disable --full-tree.

option.name: --object-only
tip: List only names of the objects, one per line.
Cannot be combined with --name-only or --name-status.

This is equivalent to specifying --format='%(objectname)', but for both this option and that exact format the command takes a hand-optimized codepath instead of going through the generic formatting mechanism.

option.name: -d
tip: Show only the named tree entry itself, not its children.

option.name: -r
tip: Recurse into sub-trees.

option.name: -t
tip: Show tree entries even when going to recurse them.
Has no effect if -r was not passed. -d implies -t.

option.name: -z
tip: \0 line termination on output and do not quote filenames.
See OUTPUT FORMAT below for more information.

next.name: mailinfo
tip: Extract patch and authorship from a single email message.

option.name: --encoding
tip: Similar to -u.
But when re-coding, the charset specified here is used instead of the one specified by i18n.commitEncoding or UTF-8.

option.name: --message-id
tip: Copy the Message-ID header at the end of the commit message.
This is useful in order to associate commits with mailing list discussions.

option.name: --no-message-id
tip: Disable --message-id.

option.name: --no-scissors
tip: Ignore scissors lines.
Useful for overriding mailinfo.scissors settings.

option.name: --quoted-cr
tip: Action when processes email messages sent with base64 or quoted-printable encoding, and the decoded lines end with a CRLF instead of a simple LF.

option.name: --scissors
tip: Remove everything in body before a scissors line (e.g. "-- >8 --").
The line represents scissors and perforation marks, and is used to request the reader to cut the message at that line.
If that line appears in the body of the message before the patch, everything before it (including the scissors line itself) is ignored when this option is used.

option.name: -b
tip: When -k is not in effect, all leading strings bracketed with [ and ] pairs are stripped.
This option limits the stripping to only the pairs whose bracketed string contains the word "PATCH".

option.name: -k
tip: Usually the program removes email cruft from the Subject: header line to extract the title line for the commit log message.
This option prevents this munging, and is most useful when used to read back git format-patch -k output.

option.name: -n
tip: Disable all charset re-coding of the metadata.

option.name: -u
tip: The commit log message, author name and author email are taken from the e-mail, and after minimally decoding MIME transfer encoding, re-coded in the charset specified by i18n.commitEncoding (defaulting to UTF-8) by transliterating them.
This used to be optional but now it is the default.

next.name: mailsplit
tip: Split an mbox file into a list of files.

option.name: --keep-cr
tip: Do not remove \r from lines ending with \r\n.

option.name: --mboxrd
tip: Input is of the "mboxrd" format and "^>+From " line escaping is reversed.

option.name: -b
tip: If any file doesn't begin with a From line, assume it is a single mail message instead of signaling an error.

option.name: -d
tip: Instead of the default 4 digits with leading zeros, different precision can be specified for the generated filenames.

option.name: -f
tip: Skip the first <nn> numbers, for example if -f3 is specified, start the numbering with 0004.

option.name: -o
tip: Directory in which to place the individual messages.

next.name: maintenance
tip: Run tasks to optimize Git repository data.

option.name: --auto
tip: When combined with the run subcommand, run maintenance tasks only if certain thresholds are met.
For example, the gc task runs when the number of loose objects exceeds the number stored in the gc.auto config setting, or when the number of pack-files exceeds the gc.autoPackLimit config setting.
Not compatible with the --schedule option.
When combined with the is-needed subcommand, check if the required thresholds are met without actually running maintenance.

option.name: --config-file
tip: With register, the config file receiving the repository registration.

option.name: --force
tip: With unregister, succeed even when the repository is not registered.

option.name: --quiet
tip: Do not report progress or other information over stderr.

option.name: --schedule
tip: When combined with the run subcommand, run maintenance tasks only if certain time conditions are met, as specified by the maintenance.<task>.schedule config value for each <task>.
This config value specifies a number of seconds since the last time that task ran, according to the maintenance.<task>.lastRun config value.
The tasks that are tested are those provided by the --task=<task> option(s) or those with maintenance.<task>.enabled set to true.

option.name: --scheduler
tip: When combined with the start subcommand, specify the scheduler for running the hourly, daily and weekly executions of git maintenance run.
Possible values for <scheduler> are auto, crontab (POSIX), systemd-timer (Linux), launchctl (macOS), and schtasks (Windows).
When auto is specified, the appropriate platform-specific scheduler is used; on Linux, systemd-timer is used if available, otherwise crontab.
Default is auto.

next.name: auto
tip: Platform scheduler (default).

next.name: crontab
tip: POSIX cron.

next.name: launchctl
tip: macOS launchd.

next.name: schtasks
tip: Windows scheduled tasks.

next.name: systemd-timer
tip: Linux systemd timer.

option.name: --task
tip: If this option is specified one or more times, then only run the specified tasks in the specified order.
If no --task=<task> arguments are specified, then only the tasks with maintenance.<task>.enabled configured as true are considered.
See the TASKS section for the list of accepted <task> values.

tip: Merge two or more development histories.

option.name: --abort
tip: Abort the current conflict resolution process, and try to reconstruct the pre-merge state.
If an autostash entry is present, apply it to the worktree.

option.name: --allow-unrelated-histories
tip: By default, git merge command refuses to merge histories that do not share a common ancestor.
This option can be used to override this safety when merging histories of two projects that started their lives independently.
As that is a very rare occasion, no configuration variable to enable this by default exists or will be added.

option.name: --autostash
tip: Automatically create a temporary stash entry before the operation begins, record it in the ref MERGE_AUTOSTASH and apply it after the operation ends.
This means that you can run the operation on a dirty worktree.
However, use with care: the final stash application after a successful merge might result in non-trivial conflicts.

option.name: --cleanup
tip: This option determines how the merge message will be cleaned up before committing.
See git-commit(1) for more details.
In addition, if the <mode> is given a value of scissors, scissors will be appended to MERGE_MSG before being passed on to the commit machinery in the case of a merge conflict.

option.name: --commit
tip: Perform the merge and commit the result.
This option can be used to override --no-commit.

option.name: --compact-summary
tip: Show a compact-summary at the end of the merge.

option.name: --continue
tip: After a git merge stops due to conflicts you can conclude the merge by running git merge --continue (see "HOW TO RESOLVE CONFLICTS" section below).

option.name: --edit
tip: Invoke an editor before committing successful mechanical merge to further edit the auto-generated merge message, so that the user can explain and justify the merge.
The --no-edit option can be used to accept the auto-generated message (this is generally discouraged).
The --edit (or -e) option is still useful if you are giving a draft message with the -m option from the command line and want to edit it in the editor.

option.name: --ff
tip: Specifies how a merge is handled when the merged-in history is already a descendant of the current history. --ff is the default unless merging an annotated (and possibly signed) tag that is not stored in its natural place in the refs/tags/ hierarchy, in which case --no-ff is assumed.

option.name: --ff-only
tip: Specifies how a merge is handled when the merged-in history is already a descendant of the current history. --ff is the default unless merging an annotated (and possibly signed) tag that is not stored in its natural place in the refs/tags/ hierarchy, in which case --no-ff is assumed.

option.name: --file
tip: Read the commit message to be used for the merge commit (in case one is created).

option.name: --gpg-sign
tip: GPG-sign the resulting merge commit.

The <key-id> argument is optional and defaults to the committer identity; if specified, it must be stuck to the option without a space. --no-gpg-sign is useful to countermand both commit.gpgSign configuration variable, and earlier --gpg-sign.

option.name: --into-name
tip: Prepare the default merge message as if merging to the branch <branch>, instead of the name of the real branch to which the merge is made.

option.name: --log
tip: In addition to branch names, populate the log message with one-line descriptions from at most <n> actual commits that are being merged.
See also git-fmt-merge-msg(1).

option.name: --no-abort
tip: Disable --abort.

option.name: --no-allow-unrelated-histories
tip: Disable --allow-unrelated-histories.

option.name: --no-autostash
tip: Automatically create a temporary stash entry before the operation begins, record it in the ref MERGE_AUTOSTASH and apply it after the operation ends.
This means that you can run the operation on a dirty worktree.
However, use with care: the final stash application after a successful merge might result in non-trivial conflicts.

option.name: --no-commit
tip: Perform the merge and commit the result.
This option can be used to override --no-commit.

option.name: --no-compact-summary
tip: Disable --compact-summary.

option.name: --no-continue
tip: Disable --continue.

option.name: --no-edit
tip: Invoke an editor before committing successful mechanical merge to further edit the auto-generated merge message, so that the user can explain and justify the merge.
The --no-edit option can be used to accept the auto-generated message (this is generally discouraged).
The --edit (or -e) option is still useful if you are giving a draft message with the -m option from the command line and want to edit it in the editor.

option.name: --no-ff
tip: Specifies how a merge is handled when the merged-in history is already a descendant of the current history. --ff is the default unless merging an annotated (and possibly signed) tag that is not stored in its natural place in the refs/tags/ hierarchy, in which case --no-ff is assumed.

option.name: --no-gpg-sign
tip: GPG-sign the resulting merge commit.

The <key-id> argument is optional and defaults to the committer identity; if specified, it must be stuck to the option without a space. --no-gpg-sign is useful to countermand both commit.gpgSign configuration variable, and earlier --gpg-sign.

option.name: --no-log
tip: In addition to branch names, populate the log message with one-line descriptions from at most <n> actual commits that are being merged.
See also git-fmt-merge-msg(1).

option.name: --no-overwrite-ignore
tip: Silently overwrite ignored files from the merge result.
This is the default behavior.
Use --no-overwrite-ignore to abort.

option.name: --no-progress
tip: Turn progress on/off explicitly.
If neither is specified, progress is shown if standard error is connected to a terminal.
Note that not all merge strategies may support progress reporting.

option.name: --no-quiet
tip: Disable --quiet.

option.name: --no-quit
tip: Disable --quit.

option.name: --no-rerere-autoupdate
tip: After the rerere mechanism reuses a recorded resolution on the current conflict to update the files in the working tree, allow it to also update the index with the result of resolution. --no-rerere-autoupdate is a good way to double-check what git-rerere(1) did and catch potential mismerges, before committing the result to the index with a separate git-add(1).

option.name: --no-signoff
tip: Add a Signed-off-by trailer by the committer at the end of the commit log message.
The meaning of a signoff depends on the project to which you're committing.
For example, it may certify that the committer has the rights to submit the work under the project's license or agrees to some contributor representation, such as a Developer Certificate of Origin.

(See https://developercertificate.org for the one used by the Linux kernel and Git projects.) Consult the documentation or leadership of the project to which you're contributing to understand how the signoffs are used in that project.

option.name: --no-squash
tip: Produce the working tree and index state as if a real merge happened (except for the merge information), but do not actually make a commit, move the HEAD, or record $GIT_DIR/MERGE_HEAD (to cause the next git commit command to create a merge commit).
This allows you to create a single commit on top of the current branch whose effect is the same as merging another branch (or more in case of an octopus).

option.name: --no-stat
tip: Show a diffstat at the end of the merge.
The diffstat is also controlled by the configuration option merge.stat.

option.name: --no-summary
tip: Synonyms to --stat and --no-stat; these are deprecated and will be removed in the future.

option.name: --no-verbose
tip: Disable --verbose.

option.name: --no-verify
tip: By default, the pre-merge and commit-msg hooks are run.
When --no-verify is given, these are bypassed.
See also githooks(5).

option.name: --no-verify-signatures
tip: Verify that the tip commit of the side branch being merged is signed with a valid key, i.e. a key that has a valid uid: in the default trust model, this means the signing key has been signed by a trusted key.
If the tip commit of the side branch is not signed with a valid key, the merge is aborted.

option.name: --overwrite-ignore
tip: Silently overwrite ignored files from the merge result.
This is the default behavior.
Use --no-overwrite-ignore to abort.

option.name: --progress
tip: Turn progress on/off explicitly.
If neither is specified, progress is shown if standard error is connected to a terminal.
Note that not all merge strategies may support progress reporting.

option.name: --quiet
tip: Operate quietly.
Implies --no-progress.

option.name: --quit
tip: Forget about the current merge in progress.
Leave the index and the working tree as-is.
If MERGE_AUTOSTASH is present, the stash entry will be saved to the stash list.

option.name: --rerere-autoupdate
tip: After the rerere mechanism reuses a recorded resolution on the current conflict to update the files in the working tree, allow it to also update the index with the result of resolution. --no-rerere-autoupdate is a good way to double-check what git-rerere(1) did and catch potential mismerges, before committing the result to the index with a separate git-add(1).
