option.name: --stat
tip: Show a diffstat at the end of the merge.
The diffstat is also controlled by the configuration option merge.stat.

option.name: --strategy
tip: Use the given merge strategy; can be supplied more than once to specify them in the order they should be tried.
If there is no -s option, a built-in list of strategies is used instead (ort when merging a single head, octopus otherwise).

next.name: octopus
tip: Resolves cases with more than two heads.

next.name: ort
tip: Default merge strategy for pulling or merging one branch.

next.name: ours
tip: Resolves any number of heads, but the resulting tree is always that of the current branch.

next.name: recursive
tip: Synonym for ort.

next.name: resolve
tip: Can only resolve two heads using a 3-way merge algorithm.

next.name: subtree
tip: A modified ort strategy, adjusted for subtree merging.

option.name: --strategy-option
tip: Pass merge strategy specific option through to the merge strategy.

next.name: diff-algorithm=(minimal|patience|histogram|myers)
tip: Use a different diff algorithm while merging.

next.name: histogram
tip: Use histogram diff algorithm.

next.name: ours
tip: Conflicting hunks are auto-resolved by favoring our version.

next.name: patience
tip: Use patience diff algorithm.

next.name: theirs
tip: Conflicting hunks are auto-resolved by favoring their version.

option.name: --summary
tip: Synonyms to --stat and --no-stat; these are deprecated and will be removed in the future.

option.name: --verbose
tip: Be verbose.

option.name: --verify
tip: By default, the pre-merge and commit-msg hooks are run.
When --no-verify is given, these are bypassed.
See also githooks(5).

option.name: --verify-signatures
tip: Verify that the tip commit of the side branch being merged is signed with a valid key, i.e. a key that has a valid uid: in the default trust model, this means the signing key has been signed by a trusted key.
If the tip commit of the side branch is not signed with a valid key, the merge is aborted.

option.name: -m
tip: Set the commit message to be used for the merge commit (in case one is created).

next.name: merge-base
tip: Find common ancestors as merge bases as cheaply as possible.

option.name: --all
tip: Output all merge bases for the commits, instead of just one.

option.name: --fork-point
tip: Find the point at which a branch (or any history that leads to <commit>) forked from another branch (or any reference) <ref>.

This does not just look for the common ancestor of the two commits, but also takes into account the reflog of <ref> to see if the history leading to <commit> forked from an earlier incarnation of the branch <ref> (see discussion of this mode below).

option.name: --independent
tip: Instead of printing merge bases, print a minimal subset of the supplied commits with the same ancestors.
In other words, among the commits given, list those which cannot be reached from any other.
This mimics the behavior of git show-branch --independent.

option.name: --is-ancestor
tip: Check if the first <commit> is an ancestor of the second <commit>, and exit with status 0 if true, or with status 1 if not.
Errors are signaled by a non-zero status that is not 1.

option.name: --no-all
tip: Disable --all.

option.name: --octopus
tip: Compute the best common ancestors of all supplied commits, in preparation for an n-way merge.
This mimics the behavior of git show-branch --merge-base.

next.name: merge-file
tip: Run a three-way file merge.

option.name: --diff-algorithm
tip: Use a different diff algorithm while merging.
The current default is "myers", but selecting more recent algorithm such as "histogram" can help avoid mismerges that occur due to unimportant matching lines (such as braces from distinct functions).
See also git-diff(1) --diff-algorithm.

option.name: --diff3
tip: Show conflicts in "diff3" style.

option.name: --no-diff3
tip: Disable --diff3.

option.name: --no-object-id
tip: Disable --object-id.

option.name: --no-ours
tip: Disable --ours.

option.name: --no-theirs
tip: Disable --theirs.

option.name: --no-union
tip: Disable --union.

option.name: --no-zdiff3
tip: Disable --zdiff3.

option.name: --object-id
tip: Specify the contents to merge as blobs in the current repository instead of files.
In this case, the operation must take place within a valid repository.

option.name: --ours
tip: Instead of leaving conflicts in the file, resolve conflicts favouring our (or their or both) side of the lines.

option.name: --theirs
tip: Instead of leaving conflicts in the file, resolve conflicts favouring our (or their or both) side of the lines.

option.name: --union
tip: Instead of leaving conflicts in the file, resolve conflicts favouring our (or their or both) side of the lines.

option.name: --zdiff3
tip: Show conflicts in "zdiff3" style.

option.name: -L
tip: This option may be given up to three times, and specifies labels to be used in place of the corresponding file names in conflict reports.
That is, git merge-file -L x -L y -L z a b c generates output that looks like it came from files x, y and z instead of from files a, b and c.

option.name: -p
tip: Send results to standard output instead of overwriting <current>.

option.name: -q
tip: Quiet; do not warn about conflicts.

next.name: merge-index
tip: Run a merge for files needing merging.

option.name: -a
tip: Run merge against all files in the index that need merging.

option.name: -o
tip: Instead of stopping at the first failed merge, do all of them in one shot - continue with merging even when previous merges returned errors, and only return the error code after all the merges.

option.name: -q
tip: Do not complain about a failed merge program (a merge program failure usually indicates conflicts during the merge).
This is for porcelains which might want to emit custom messages.

next.name: merge-octopus
tip: Internal merge strategy driver that handles more than two heads.

next.name: merge-one-file
tip: Common core of 'git merge-index' and standard helper for use with git merge-index.

next.name: merge-ours
tip: Internal merge strategy driver that keeps our version.

next.name: merge-recursive
tip: Internal recursive merge strategy driver.

next.name: merge-recursive-ours
tip: Recursive merge strategy driver that keeps our version.

next.name: merge-recursive-theirs
tip: Recursive merge strategy driver that keeps their version.

next.name: merge-resolve
tip: Internal merge strategy driver that uses a temporary tree.

next.name: merge-subtree
tip: Internal merge strategy driver that performs a subtree merge.

next.name: merge-tree
tip: Show three-way merge without touching the index.

option.name: --allow-unrelated-histories
tip: merge-tree will by default error out if the two branches specified share no common history.
This flag can be given to override that check and make the merge proceed anyway.

option.name: --merge-base
tip: Instead of finding the merge-bases for <branch1> and <branch2>, specify a merge-base for the merge.
This option is incompatible with --stdin.

option.name: --messages
tip: Write any informational messages such as "Auto-merging <path>" or CONFLICT notices to the end of stdout.
If unspecified, the default is to include these messages if there are merge conflicts, and to omit them otherwise.

option.name: --name-only
tip: In the Conflicted file info section, instead of writing a list of (mode, oid, stage, path) tuples to output for conflicted files, just provide a list of filenames with conflicts (and do not list filenames multiple times if they have multiple conflicting stages).

option.name: --no-messages
tip: Write any informational messages such as "Auto-merging <path>" or CONFLICT notices to the end of stdout.
If unspecified, the default is to include these messages if there are merge conflicts, and to omit them otherwise.

option.name: --quiet
tip: Disable all output from the program.
Useful when you are only interested in the exit status.
Allows merge-tree to exit early when it finds a conflict, and allows it to avoid writing most objects created by merges.

option.name: --stdin
tip: Read the commits to merge from the standard input rather than the command-line.
See INPUT FORMAT below for more information.
Implies -z.

option.name: --strategy-option
tip: Pass the merge strategy-specific option through to the merge strategy.
See git-merge(1) for details.

option.name: -z
tip: Do not quote filenames in the <Conflicted file info> section, and end each filename with a NUL character rather than newline.
Also begin the messages section with a NUL character instead of a newline.
See OUTPUT below for more information.

next.name: mergetool
tip: Run merge conflict resolution tools to resolve merge conflicts.

option.name: --gui
tip: When git-mergetool is invoked with the -g or --gui option, the default merge tool will be read from the configured merge.guitool variable instead of merge.tool.
If merge.guitool is not set, we will fallback to the tool configured under merge.tool.
This may be autoselected using the configuration variable mergetool.guiDefault.

option.name: --no-gui
tip: This overrides a previous -g or --gui setting or mergetool.guiDefault configuration and reads the default merge tool from the configured merge.tool variable.

option.name: --no-prompt
tip: Don't prompt before each invocation of the merge resolution program.
This is the default if the merge resolution program is explicitly specified with the --tool option or with the merge.tool configuration variable.

option.name: --no-tool-help
tip: Disable --tool-help.

option.name: --prompt
tip: Prompt before each invocation of the merge resolution program to give the user a chance to skip the path.

option.name: --tool
tip: Use the merge resolution program specified by <tool>.
Valid values include emerge, gvimdiff, kdiff3, meld, vimdiff, and tortoisemerge.
Run git mergetool --tool-help for the list of valid <tool> settings.

option.name: --tool-help
tip: Print a list of merge tools that may be used with --tool.

option.name: -O
tip: Process files in the order specified in the <orderfile>, which has one shell glob pattern per line.
This overrides the diff.orderFile configuration variable (see git-config(1)).
To cancel diff.orderFile, use -O/dev/null.

next.name: mktag
tip: Create a tag object with optional verification.

option.name: --no-strict
tip: Disable --strict.

option.name: --strict
tip: By default mktag turns on the equivalent of git-fsck(1) --strict mode.
Use --no-strict to disable it.

next.name: mktree
tip: Build a tree-object from ls-tree formatted text.

option.name: --batch
tip: Allow building of more than one tree object before exiting.
Each tree is separated by a single blank line.
The final newline is optional.
Note - if the -z option is used, lines are terminated with NUL.

option.name: --missing
tip: Allow missing objects.
The default behaviour (without this option) is to verify that each tree entry's hash identifies an existing object.
This option has no effect on the treatment of gitlink entries (aka "submodules") which are always allowed to be missing.

option.name: --no-batch
tip: Disable --batch.

option.name: --no-missing
tip: Disable --missing.

option.name: -z
tip: Read the NUL-terminated ls-tree -z output instead.

option.name: --batch-size
tip: With repack, select small pack-files up to the expected batch size.

option.name: --bitmap

tip: Update the chain file normally.

tip: The internal block size to use when converting a revision specifier such as @all into a list of specific change numbers.

option.name: --changesfile
tip: Import exactly the p4 change numbers listed in file, one per line.

option.name: --commit
tip: Submit only the specified commit or range of commits, instead of the full list of changes that are in the current Git branch.

option.name: --conflict
tip: Conflicts can occur when applying a commit to p4.

next.name: quit

option.name: --import-labels

option.name: --silent

option.name: --update-shelve

tip: Create a packed archive of objects.

option.name: --all
tip: This implies --revs.
In addition to the list of revision arguments read from the standard input, pretend as if all refs under refs/ are specified to be included.

option.name: --all-progress
tip: When --stdout is specified then progress report is displayed during the object count and compression phases but inhibited during the write-out phase.
The reason is that in some cases the output stream is directly linked to another command which may wish to display progress status of its own as it processes incoming pack data.
This flag is like --progress except that it forces progress report for the write-out phase as well even if --stdout is used.

option.name: --all-progress-implied
tip: This is used to imply --all-progress whenever progress display is activated.
Unlike --all-progress this flag doesn't actually force any progress display by itself.

option.name: --compression
tip: Specifies compression level for newly-compressed data in the generated pack.
If not specified, pack compression level is determined first by pack.compression, then by core.compression, and defaults to -1, the zlib default, if neither is set.
Add --no-reuse-object if you want to force a uniform compression level on all data no matter the source.

option.name: --cruft
tip: Packs unreachable objects into a separate "cruft" pack, denoted by the existence of a .mtimes file.
Typically used by git repack --cruft.
Callers provide a list of pack names and indicate which packs will remain in the repository, along with which packs will be deleted (indicated by the - prefix).

The contents of the cruft pack are all objects not contained in the surviving packs which have not exceeded the grace period (see --cruft-expiration below), or which have exceeded the grace period, but are reachable from an other object which hasn't.

option.name: --cruft-expiration
tip: If specified, objects are eliminated from the cruft pack if they have an mtime older than <approxidate>.
If unspecified (and given --cruft), then no objects are eliminated.

option.name: --delta-base-offset
tip: A packed archive can express the base object of a delta as either a 20-byte object name or as an offset in the stream, but ancient versions of Git don't understand the latter.
By default, git pack-objects only uses the former format for better compatibility.
This option allows the command to use the latter format for compactness.
Depending on the average delta chain length, this option typically shrinks the resulting packfile by 3-5 per-cent.

option.name: --delta-islands
tip: Restrict delta matches based on "islands".
See DELTA ISLANDS below.

option.name: --depth
tip: These two options affect how the objects contained in the pack are stored using delta compression.

The objects are first internally sorted by type, size and optionally names and compared against the other objects within --window to see if using delta compression saves space. --depth limits the maximum delta depth; making it too deep affects the performance on the unpacker side, because delta data needs to be applied that many times to get to the necessary object.

option.name: --exclude
tip: Do not include objects matching the given pattern.
This is useful for excluding certain files from the pack.

option.name: --exclude-promisor-objects
tip: Omit objects that are known to be in the promisor remote.

(This option has the purpose of operating only on locally created objects, so that when we repack, we still maintain a distinction between locally created objects [without .promisor] and objects from the promisor remote [with .promisor].) This is used with partial clone.

option.name: --filter
tip: Omits certain objects (usually blobs) from the resulting packfile.
See git-rev-list(1) for valid <filter-spec> forms.

option.name: --honor-pack-keep
tip: This flag causes an object already in a local pack that has a .keep file to be ignored, even if it would have otherwise been packed.

option.name: --include-tag
tip: Include unasked-for annotated tags if the object they reference was included in the resulting packfile.
This can be useful to send new tags to native Git clients.

option.name: --incremental
tip: This flag causes an object already in a pack to be ignored even if it would have otherwise been packed.

option.name: --index-version
tip: This is intended to be used by the test suite only.
It allows to force the version for the generated pack index, and to force 64-bit index entries on objects located above the given offset.

option.name: --keep-pack
tip: This flag causes an object already in the given pack to be ignored, even if it would have otherwise been packed. <pack-name> is the pack file name without leading directory (e.g. pack-123.pack).
The option could be specified multiple times to keep multiple packs.

option.name: --keep-true-parents
tip: With this option, parents that are hidden by grafts are packed nevertheless.

option.name: --keep-unreachable
tip: Objects unreachable from the refs in packs named with --unpacked= option are added to the resulting pack, in addition to the reachable objects that are not in packs marked with *.keep files.
This implies --revs.

option.name: --local
tip: This flag causes an object that is borrowed from an alternate object store to be ignored even if it would have otherwise been packed.

option.name: --max-pack-size
tip: In unusual scenarios, you may not be able to create files larger than a certain size on your filesystem, and this option can be used to tell the command to split the output packfile into multiple independent packfiles, each not larger than the given size.
The size can be suffixed with "k", "m", or "g".
The minimum size allowed is limited to 1 MiB.
The default is unlimited, unless the config variable pack.packSizeLimit is set.

option.name: --missing
tip: A debug option to help with future "partial clone" development.
This option specifies how missing objects are handled.

option.name: --name-hash-version
tip: While performing delta compression, Git groups objects that may be similar based on heuristics using the path to that object.
While grouping objects by an exact path match is good for paths with many versions, there are benefits for finding delta pairs across different full paths.
Git collects objects by type and then by a "name hash" of the path and then by size, hoping to group objects that will compress well together.

tip: When creating a packed archive in a repository that has existing packs, the command reuses existing deltas.
This sometimes results in a slightly suboptimal pack.
This flag tells the command not to reuse existing deltas but compute them from scratch.

option.name: --no-reuse-object
tip: This flag tells the command not to reuse existing object data at all, including non deltified object, forcing recompression of everything.
This implies --no-reuse-delta.
Useful only in the obscure case where wholesale enforcement of a different compression level on the packed data is desired.

option.name: --progress
tip: Progress status is reported on the standard error stream by default when it is attached to a terminal, unless -q is specified.
This flag forces progress status even if the standard error stream is not directed to a terminal.

option.name: --revs
tip: Read the revision arguments from the standard input, instead of individual object names.
The revision arguments are processed the same way as git rev-list with the --objects flag uses its commit arguments to build the list of objects it outputs.
The objects on the resulting list are packed.
Besides revisions, --not or --shallow <SHA-1> lines are also accepted.

option.name: --shallow
tip: Optimize a pack that will be provided to a client with a shallow repository.
This option, combined with --thin, can result in a smaller pack at the cost of speed.

option.name: --sparse
tip: Toggle the "sparse" algorithm to determine which objects to include in the pack, when combined with the "--revs" option.
This algorithm only walks trees that appear in paths that introduce new objects.
This can have significant performance benefits when computing a pack to send a small change.
However, it is possible that extra objects are added to the pack-file if the included commits contain certain types of direct renames.

option.name: --stdin-packs
tip: Read the basenames of packfiles (e.g., pack-1234abcd.pack) from the standard input, instead of object names or revision arguments.
The resulting pack contains all objects listed in the included packs (those not beginning with ^), excluding any objects listed in the excluded packs (beginning with ^).

option.name: --stdout
tip: Write the pack contents (what would have been written to .pack file) out to the standard output.

option.name: --thin
tip: Create a "thin" pack by omitting the common objects between a sender and a receiver in order to reduce network transfer.
This option only makes sense in conjunction with --stdout.

option.name: --threads
tip: Specifies the number of threads to spawn when searching for best delta matches.
This requires that pack-objects be compiled with pthreads otherwise this option is ignored with a warning.
This is meant to reduce packing time on multiprocessor machines.
The required amount of memory for the delta search window is however multiplied by the number of threads.

tip: Keep unreachable objects in loose form.
This implies --revs.

option.name: --unpacked
tip: This implies --revs.

option.name: --window
tip: These two options affect how the objects contained in the pack are stored using delta compression.

The objects are first internally sorted by type, size and optionally names and compared against the other objects within --window to see if using delta compression saves space. --depth limits the maximum delta depth; making it too deep affects the performance on the unpacker side, because delta data needs to be applied that many times to get to the necessary object.

option.name: --window-memory
tip: This option provides an additional limit on top of --window; the window size will dynamically scale down so as to not take up more than <n> bytes in memory.
This is useful in repositories with a mix of large and small objects to not run out of memory with a large window, but still be able to take advantage of the large window for the smaller objects.
The size can be suffixed with "k", "m", or "g". --window-memory=0 makes memory usage unlimited.
The default is taken from the pack.windowMemory configuration variable.

tip: Fetch and merge from another repository or local branch.

option.name: --all
tip: Fetch all remotes, except for the ones that have the remote.<name>.skipFetchAll configuration variable set.
This overrides the configuration variable fetch.all.

option.name: --allow-unrelated-histories
tip: By default, git merge command refuses to merge histories that do not share a common ancestor.
This option can be used to override this safety when merging histories of two projects that started their lives independently.
As that is a very rare occasion, no configuration variable to enable this by default exists or will be added.

option.name: --append
tip: Append ref names and object names of fetched refs to the existing contents of .git/FETCH_HEAD.
Without this option old data in .git/FETCH_HEAD will be overwritten.

option.name: --atomic
tip: Use an atomic transaction to update local refs.
Either all refs are updated, or on error, no refs are updated.

option.name: --autostash
tip: Automatically create a temporary stash entry before the operation begins, record it in the ref MERGE_AUTOSTASH and apply it after the operation ends.
This means that you can run the operation on a dirty worktree.
However, use with care: the final stash application after a successful merge might result in non-trivial conflicts.

option.name: --cleanup
tip: This option determines how the merge message will be cleaned up before committing.
See git-commit(1) for more details.
In addition, if the <mode> is given a value of scissors, scissors will be appended to MERGE_MSG before being passed on to the commit machinery in the case of a merge conflict.

option.name: --commit
tip: Perform the merge and commit the result.
This option can be used to override --no-commit.
Only useful when merging.

option.name: --compact-summary
tip: Show a compact-summary at the end of the merge.

option.name: --deepen
tip: Similar to --depth, except it specifies the number of commits from the current shallow boundary instead of from the tip of each remote branch history.

option.name: --depth
tip: Limit fetching to the specified number of commits from the tip of each remote branch history.
If fetching to a shallow repository created by git clone with --depth=<depth> option (see git-clone(1)), deepen or shorten the history to the specified number of commits.
Tags for the deepened commits are not fetched.

option.name: --dry-run
tip: Show what would be done, without making any changes.

option.name: --edit
tip: Invoke an editor before committing successful mechanical merge to further edit the auto-generated merge message, so that the user can explain and justify the merge.
The --no-edit option can be used to accept the auto-generated message (this is generally discouraged).

option.name: --ff
tip: When merging rather than rebasing, specifies how a merge is handled when the merged-in history is already a descendant of the current history.

If merging is requested, --ff is the default unless merging an annotated (and possibly signed) tag that is not stored in its natural place in the refs/tags/ hierarchy, in which case --no-ff is assumed.

option.name: --ff-only
tip: Only update to the new history if there is no divergent local history.
This is the default when no method for reconciling divergent histories is provided (via the --rebase flags).

option.name: --filter
tip: Use the partial clone feature and request that the server sends a subset of reachable objects according to a given object filter.
When using --filter, the supplied <filter-spec> is used for the partial fetch.

option.name: --force
tip: When git fetch is used with <src>:<dst> refspec, it may refuse to update the local branch as discussed in the <refspec> part of the git-fetch(1) documentation.
This option overrides that check.

option.name: --gpg-sign
tip: GPG-sign the resulting merge commit.

The <key-id> argument is optional and defaults to the committer identity; if specified, it must be stuck to the option without a space. --no-gpg-sign is useful to countermand both commit.gpgSign configuration variable, and earlier --gpg-sign.

option.name: --ipv4
tip: Use IPv4 addresses only, ignoring IPv6 addresses.

option.name: --ipv6
tip: Use IPv6 addresses only, ignoring IPv4 addresses.

option.name: --jobs
tip: Parallelize all forms of fetching up to <n> jobs at a time.

option.name: --keep
tip: Keep downloaded pack.

option.name: --log
tip: In addition to branch names, populate the log message with one-line descriptions from at most <n> actual commits that are being merged.
See also git-fmt-merge-msg(1).
Only useful when merging.

option.name: --negotiate-only
tip: Do not fetch anything from the server, and instead print the ancestors of the provided --negotiation-restrict= arguments, which we have in common with the server.

option.name: --negotiation-include
tip: Ensure that the commits at the given tips are always sent as "have" lines during fetch negotiation, regardless of what the negotiation algorithm selects.

This is useful to guarantee that common history reachable from specific refs is always considered, even when --negotiation-restrict restricts the set of tips or when the negotiation algorithm would otherwise skip them.

option.name: --negotiation-restrict
tip: By default, Git will report, to the server, commits reachable from all local refs to find common commits in an attempt to reduce the size of the to-be-received packfile.
If specified, Git will only report commits reachable from the given tips.
This is useful to speed up fetches when the user knows which local ref is likely to have commits in common with the upstream ref being fetched.

option.name: --negotiation-tip
tip: By default, Git will report, to the server, commits reachable from all local refs to find common commits in an attempt to reduce the size of the to-be-received packfile.
If specified, Git will only report commits reachable from the given tips.
This is useful to speed up fetches when the user knows which local ref is likely to have commits in common with the upstream ref being fetched.

option.name: --no-all
tip: Fetch all remotes, except for the ones that have the remote.<name>.skipFetchAll configuration variable set.
This overrides the configuration variable fetch.all.

option.name: --no-allow-unrelated-histories
tip: Disable --allow-unrelated-histories.

option.name: --no-append

option.name: --no-autostash

option.name: --no-force
tip: Disable --force.

option.name: --no-gpg-sign
tip: GPG-sign the resulting merge commit.

option.name: --no-ipv6

option.name: --no-recurse-submodules
tip: This option controls if new commits of populated submodules should be fetched, and if the working trees of active submodules should be updated, too (see git-fetch(1), git-config(1) and gitmodules(5)).

option.name: --no-set-upstream
tip: Disable --set-upstream.

option.name: --no-show-forced-updates
tip: By default, git checks if a branch is force-updated during fetch.
Pass --no-show-forced-updates or set fetch.showForcedUpdates to false to skip this check for performance reasons.
If used during git-pull the --ff-only option will still check for forced updates before attempting a fast-forward update.
See git-config(1).

option.name: --no-signoff
tip: Add a Signed-off-by trailer by the committer at the end of the commit log message.
The meaning of a signoff depends on the project to which you're committing.
For example, it may certify that the committer has the rights to submit the work under the project's license or agrees to some contributor representation, such as a Developer Certificate of Origin.

(See https://developercertificate.org for the one used by the Linux kernel and Git projects.) Consult the documentation or leadership of the project to which you're contributing to understand how the signoffs are used in that project.

option.name: --no-squash
tip: Produce the working tree and index state as if a real merge happened (except for the merge information), but do not actually make a commit, move the HEAD, or record $GIT_DIR/MERGE_HEAD (to cause the next git commit command to create a merge commit).
This allows you to create a single commit on top of the current branch whose effect is the same as merging another branch (or more in case of an octopus).

option.name: --no-stat
tip: Show a diffstat at the end of the merge.
The diffstat is also controlled by the configuration option merge.stat.

option.name: --no-summary
tip: Synonyms to --stat and --no-stat; these are deprecated and will be removed in the future.

option.name: --no-tags
tip: By default, tags that point at objects that are downloaded from the remote repository are fetched and stored locally.
This option disables this automatic tag following.
The default behavior for a remote may be specified with the remote.<name>.tagOpt setting.
See git-config(1).

option.name: --no-update-shallow
tip: Disable --update-shallow.

option.name: --no-verbose

option.name: --no-verify
tip: By default, the pre-merge and commit-msg hooks are run.
When --no-verify is given, these are bypassed.
See also githooks(5).
Only useful when merging.

option.name: --no-verify-signatures
tip: Verify that the tip commit of the side branch being merged is signed with a valid key, i.e. a key that has a valid uid: in the default trust model, this means the signing key has been signed by a trusted key.
If the tip commit of the side branch is not signed with a valid key, the merge is aborted.

option.name: --porcelain
tip: Print the output to standard output in an easy-to-parse format for scripts.
See section OUTPUT in git-fetch(1) for details.

option.name: --prefetch
tip: Modify the configured refspec to place all refs into the refs/prefetch/ namespace.
See the prefetch task in git-maintenance(1).

option.name: --progress
tip: Progress status is reported on the standard error stream by default when it is attached to a terminal, unless -q is specified.
This flag forces progress status even if the standard error stream is not directed to a terminal.

option.name: --prune
tip: Before fetching, remove any remote-tracking references that no longer exist on the remote.
Tags are not subject to pruning if they are fetched only because of the default tag auto-following or due to a --tags option.

However, if tags are fetched due to an explicit refspec (either on the command line or in the remote configuration, for example if the remote was cloned with the --mirror option), then they are also subject to pruning.
Supplying --prune-tags is a shorthand for providing the tag refspec.

option.name: --quiet
tip: This is passed to both underlying git-fetch to squelch reporting of during transfer, and underlying git-merge to squelch output during merging.

option.name: --rebase
tip: true rebase the current branch on top of the upstream branch after fetching.
If there is a remote-tracking branch corresponding to the upstream branch and the upstream branch was rebased since last fetched, the rebase uses that information to avoid rebasing non-local changes.
This is the default.

option.name: --recurse-submodules
tip: This option controls if new commits of populated submodules should be fetched, and if the working trees of active submodules should be updated, too (see git-fetch(1), git-config(1) and gitmodules(5)).

next.name: no

next.name: on-demand

next.name: yes

option.name: --refmap
tip: When fetching refs listed on the command line, use the specified refspec (can be given more than once) to map the refs to remote-tracking branches, instead of the values of remote.<name>.fetch configuration variables for the remote repository.
Providing an empty <refspec> to the --refmap option causes Git to ignore the configured refspecs and rely entirely on the refspecs supplied as command-line arguments.
See section on "Configured Remote-tracking Branches" for details.

option.name: --server-option
tip: Transmit the given string to the server when communicating using protocol version 2.
The given string must not contain a NUL or LF character.
The server's handling of server options, including unknown ones, is server-specific.
When multiple --server-option=<option> are given, they are all sent to the other side in the order listed on the command line.

option.name: --set-upstream
tip: If the remote is fetched successfully, add upstream (tracking) reference, used by argument-less git-pull(1) and other commands.
For more information, see branch.<name>.merge and branch.<name>.remote in git-config(1).

option.name: --shallow-exclude
tip: Deepen or shorten the history of a shallow repository to exclude commits reachable from a specified remote branch or tag.
This option can be specified multiple times.

option.name: --shallow-since
tip: Deepen or shorten the history of a shallow repository to include all reachable commits after <date>.

option.name: --show-forced-updates
tip: By default, git checks if a branch is force-updated during fetch.
This can be disabled through fetch.showForcedUpdates, but the --show-forced-updates option guarantees this check occurs.
See git-config(1).

option.name: --signoff
tip: Add a Signed-off-by trailer by the committer at the end of the commit log message.
The meaning of a signoff depends on the project to which you're committing.
For example, it may certify that the committer has the rights to submit the work under the project's license or agrees to some contributor representation, such as a Developer Certificate of Origin.

(See https://developercertificate.org for the one used by the Linux kernel and Git projects.) Consult the documentation or leadership of the project to which you're contributing to understand how the signoffs are used in that project.

option.name: --squash
tip: Produce the working tree and index state as if a real merge happened (except for the merge information), but do not actually make a commit, move the HEAD, or record $GIT_DIR/MERGE_HEAD (to cause the next git commit command to create a merge commit).
This allows you to create a single commit on top of the current branch whose effect is the same as merging another branch (or more in case of an octopus).

option.name: --stat
tip: Show a diffstat at the end of the merge.
The diffstat is also controlled by the configuration option merge.stat.

option.name: --strategy
tip: Use the given merge strategy; can be supplied more than once to specify them in the order they should be tried.
If there is no -s option, a built-in list of strategies is used instead (ort when merging a single head, octopus otherwise).

next.name: octopus
tip: Resolves cases with more than two heads.

next.name: ort
tip: Default merge strategy for pulling or merging one branch.

next.name: ours
tip: Resolves any number of heads, but the resulting tree is always that of the current branch.

next.name: recursive
tip: Synonym for ort.

next.name: resolve
tip: Can only resolve two heads using a 3-way merge algorithm.

next.name: subtree
tip: A modified ort strategy, adjusted for subtree merging.

option.name: --strategy-option
tip: Pass merge strategy specific option through to the merge strategy.

option.name: --summary
tip: Synonyms to --stat and --no-stat; these are deprecated and will be removed in the future.

option.name: --tags
tip: Fetch all tags from the remote (i.e., fetch remote tags refs/tags/* into local tags with the same name), in addition to whatever else would otherwise be fetched.
Using this option alone does not subject tags to pruning, even if --prune is used (though tags may be pruned anyway if they are also the destination of an explicit refspec; see --prune).

option.name: --unshallow
tip: If the source repository is complete, convert a shallow repository to a complete one, removing all the limitations imposed by shallow repositories.

option.name: --update-shallow
tip: By default when fetching from a shallow repository, git fetch refuses refs that require updating .git/shallow.
This option updates .git/shallow and accepts such refs.

option.name: --upload-pack
tip: When given, and the repository to fetch from is handled by git fetch-pack, --exec=<upload-pack> is passed to the command to specify non-default path for the command run on the other end.

option.name: --verbose
tip: Pass --verbose to git-fetch and git-merge.

When --no-verify is given, these are bypassed.

If the tip commit of the side branch is not signed with a valid key, the merge is aborted.

option.name: --branches

This can also be specified with configuration variable push.followTags.
For more information, see push.followTags in git-config(1).

option.name: --force-with-lease

option.name: --combine-cruft-below-size
tip: When generating cruft packs without pruning, only repack existing cruft packs whose size is strictly less than <n> bytes, which can optionally be suffixed with "k", "m", or "g".
Cruft packs whose size is greater than or equal to <n> are left as-is and not repacked.
Useful when you want to avoid repacking large cruft pack(s) in repositories that have many and/or large unreachable objects.

option.name: --cruft
tip: Same as -a, unless -d is used.
Then any unreachable objects are packed into a separate cruft pack.
Unreachable objects can be pruned using the normal expiry rules with the next git gc invocation (see git-gc(1)).
Incompatible with -k.

option.name: --cruft-expiration
tip: Expire unreachable objects older than <approxidate> immediately instead of waiting for the next git gc invocation.
Only useful with --cruft -d.

option.name: --delta-islands
tip: Pass the --delta-islands option to git-pack-objects, see git-pack-objects(1).

option.name: --depth
tip: These two options affect how the objects contained in the pack are stored using delta compression.

The objects are first internally sorted by type, size and optionally names and compared against the other objects within --window to see if using delta compression saves space. --depth limits the maximum delta depth; making it too deep affects the performance on the unpacker side, because delta data needs to be applied that many times to get to the necessary object.

option.name: --drop-filtered
tip: Delete the local objects that match the --filter specification instead of keeping them in a separate packfile, reclaiming the disk space they occupy.
This is intended for partial clones, where the filtered objects are promisor objects that remain recoverable from the promisor remote and are lazily re-fetched on demand when they are next needed.

option.name: --dry-run
tip: Only meaningful with --drop-filtered.
List the objects that would be dropped, one object ID per line, without rebuilding any pack or deleting anything.

option.name: --expire-to
tip: Write a cruft pack containing pruned objects (if any) to the directory <dir>.
This option is useful for keeping a copy of any pruned objects in a separate directory as a backup.
Only useful with --cruft -d.

option.name: --filter
tip: Remove objects matching the filter specification from the resulting packfile and put them into a separate packfile.
Note that objects used in the working directory are not filtered out.
So for the split to fully work, it's best to perform it in a bare repo and to use the -a and -d options along with this option.

Also --no-write-bitmap-index (or the repack.writebitmaps config option set to false) should be used otherwise writing bitmap index will fail, as it supposes a single packfile containing all the objects.

option.name: --filter-to
tip: Write the pack containing filtered out objects to the directory <dir>.
Only useful with --filter.
This can be used for putting the pack on a separate object directory that is accessed through the Git alternates mechanism.
WARNING: If the packfile containing the filtered out objects is not accessible, the repo can become corrupt as it might not be possible to access the objects in that packfile.

option.name: --geometric
tip: Arrange resulting pack structure so that each successive pack contains at least <factor> times the number of objects as the next-largest pack.

option.name: --keep-pack
tip: Exclude the given pack from repacking.
This is the equivalent of having .keep file on the pack. <pack-name> is the pack file name without leading directory (e.g. pack-123.pack).
The option can be specified multiple times to keep multiple packs.

option.name: --keep-unreachable
tip: When used with -ad, any unreachable objects from existing packs will be appended to the end of the packfile instead of being removed.
In addition, any unreachable loose objects will be packed (and their loose counterparts removed).

option.name: --max-cruft-size
tip: Override --max-pack-size for cruft packs.
Inherits the value of --max-pack-size (if any) by default.
See the documentation for --max-pack-size for more details.

option.name: --max-pack-size
tip: Maximum size of each output pack file.
The size can be suffixed with "k", "m", or "g".
The minimum size allowed is limited to 1 MiB.
If specified, multiple packfiles may be created, which also prevents the creation of a bitmap index.

option.name: --name-hash-version
tip: Provide this argument to the underlying git pack-objects process.
See git-pack-objects(1) for full details.

tip: Disable --cruft.

option.name: --no-delta-islands
tip: Disable --delta-islands.

option.name: --no-drop-filtered
tip: Disable --drop-filtered.

option.name: --no-dry-run
tip: Disable --dry-run.

option.name: --no-keep-unreachable
tip: Disable --keep-unreachable.

tip: Disable --pack-kept-objects.

option.name: --no-path-walk
tip: Disable --path-walk.

option.name: --no-quiet
tip: Disable --quiet.

option.name: --no-write-bitmap-index
tip: Do not write a bitmap index.
Use this when splitting the repository into multiple packs with --filter.

option.name: --pack-kept-objects
tip: Include objects in .keep files when repacking.
Note that we still do not delete .keep packs after pack-objects finishes.
This means that we may duplicate objects, but this makes the option safe to use when there are concurrent pushes or fetches.
This option is generally only useful if you are writing bitmaps with -b or repack.writeBitmaps, as it ensures that the bitmapped packfile has the necessary objects.

option.name: --path-walk
tip: Pass the --path-walk option to the underlying git pack-objects process.
See git-pack-objects(1) for full details.

option.name: --quiet
tip: Show no progress over the standard error stream and pass the -q option to git pack-objects.
See git-pack-objects(1).

option.name: --threads
tip: This option is passed through to git pack-objects.

option.name: --unpack-unreachable
tip: When loosening unreachable objects, do not bother loosening any objects older than <when>.
This can be used to optimize out the write of any objects that would be immediately pruned by a follow-up git prune.

option.name: --window
tip: These two options affect how the objects contained in the pack are stored using delta compression.

The objects are first internally sorted by type, size and optionally names and compared against the other objects within --window to see if using delta compression saves space. --depth limits the maximum delta depth; making it too deep affects the performance on the unpacker side, because delta data needs to be applied that many times to get to the necessary object.

option.name: --window-memory
tip: This option provides an additional limit on top of --window; the window size will dynamically scale down so as to not take up more than <n> bytes in memory.
This is useful in repositories with a mix of large and small objects to not run out of memory with a large window, but still be able to take advantage of the large window for the smaller objects.
The size can be suffixed with "k", "m", or "g". --window-memory=0 makes memory usage unlimited.
The default is taken from the pack.windowMemory configuration variable.

option.name: --write-bitmap-index
tip: Write a reachability bitmap index as part of the repack.
This only makes sense when used with -a, -A or -m, as the bitmaps must be able to refer to all reachable objects.
This option overrides the setting of repack.writeBitmaps.
This option has no effect if multiple packfiles are created, unless writing a MIDX (in which case a multi-pack bitmap is created).

option.name: --write-midx
tip: Write a multi-pack index (see git-multi-pack-index(1)) containing the non-redundant packs.
The following modes are available:

option.name: -a
tip: Instead of incrementally packing the unpacked objects, pack everything referenced into a single pack.
Especially useful when packing a repository that is used for private development.
Use with -d.
This will clean up the objects that git prune leaves behind, but git fsck --full --dangling shows as dangling.

option.name: -A
tip: Same as -a, unless -d is used.
Then any unreachable objects in a previous pack become loose, unpacked objects, instead of being left in the old pack.
Unreachable objects are never intentionally added to a pack, even when repacking.
This option prevents unreachable objects from being immediately deleted by way of being left in the old pack and then removed.

option.name: -d
tip: After packing, if the newly created packs make some existing packs redundant, remove the redundant packs.
Also run git prune-packed to remove redundant loose object files.

option.name: -f
tip: Pass the --no-reuse-delta option to git-pack-objects, see git-pack-objects(1).

option.name: -F
tip: Pass the --no-reuse-object option to git-pack-objects, see git-pack-objects(1).

option.name: -l
tip: Pass the --local option to git pack-objects.
See git-pack-objects(1).

option.name: -n
tip: Do not update the server information with git update-server-info.
This option skips updating local catalog files needed to publish this repository (or a direct copy of it) over HTTP or FTP.
See git-update-server-info(1).

option.name: --convert-graft-file
tip: Creates graft commits for all entries in $GIT_DIR/info/grafts and deletes that file upon success.

option.name: --delete
tip: Delete existing replace refs for the given objects.

option.name: --edit
tip: Edit an object's content interactively.
The existing content for <object> is pretty-printed into a temporary file, an editor is launched on the file, and the result is parsed to create a new object of the same type as <object>.
A replacement ref is then created to replace <object> with the newly created object.
See git-var(1) for details about how the editor will be chosen.

option.name: --force
tip: If an existing replace ref for the same object exists, it will be overwritten (instead of failing).

option.name: --format
tip: When listing, use the specified <format>, which can be one of short, medium and long.
When omitted, the format defaults to short.

option.name: --graft
tip: Create a graft commit.
A new commit is created with the same content as <commit> except that its parents will be [<parent>...:] instead of <commit>'s parents.
A replacement ref is then created to replace <commit> with the newly created commit.
Use --convert-graft-file to convert a $GIT_DIR/info/grafts file and use replace refs instead.

option.name: --list
tip: List replace refs for objects that match the given pattern (or all if no pattern is given).
Typing "git replace" without arguments, also lists all replace refs.

option.name: --no-force
tip: Disable --force.

option.name: --no-raw
tip: Disable --raw.

option.name: --raw
tip: When editing, provide the raw object contents rather than pretty-printed ones.
Currently this only affects trees, which will be shown in their binary form.
This is harder to work with, but can help when repairing a tree that is so corrupted it cannot be pretty-printed.
Note that you may need to configure your editor to cleanly read and write binary data.

tip: Show commits more recent than <date>.

option.name: --all

option.name: --all-match

option.name: --alternate-refs

The set of included objects may be modified by core.alternateRefsCommand, etc. See git-config(1).

option.name: --ancestry-path
tip: When given a range of commits to display (e.g. <commit1>..<commit2> or <commit2> ^<commit1>), and a commit <commit> in that range, only display commits in that range that are ancestors of <commit>, descendants of <commit>, or <commit> itself.
If no commit is specified, use <commit1> (the excluded part of the range) as <commit>.
Can be passed multiple times; if so, a commit is included if it is any of the commits given or if it is an ancestor or descendant of one of them.

option.name: --author
tip: Limit the commits output to ones with author/committer header lines that match the <pattern> regular expression.
With more than one --author=<pattern>, commits whose author matches any of the <pattern> are chosen (similarly for multiple --committer=<pattern>).

option.name: --author-date-order
tip: Show no parents before all of its children are shown, but otherwise show commits in the author timestamp order.

option.name: --basic-regexp

option.name: --before
tip: Show commits older than <date>.

option.name: --bisect
tip: Pretend as if the bad bisection ref refs/bisect/bad was listed and as if it was followed by --not and the good bisection refs refs/bisect/good-* on the command line.

option.name: --boundary

option.name: --branches
tip: Pretend as if all the refs in refs/heads are listed on the command line as <commit>.

option.name: --cherry

With more than one --author=<pattern>, commits whose author matches any of the <pattern> are chosen (similarly for multiple --committer=<pattern>).

option.name: --count
tip: Print a number stating how many commits would have been listed, and suppress all other output.
When used together with --left-right, instead print the counts for left and right commits, separated by a tab.
When used together with --cherry-mark, omit patch equivalent commits from these counts and print the count for equivalent commits separated by a tab.

option.name: --date
tip: Only takes effect for dates shown in human-readable format, such as when using --pretty. log.date config variable sets a default value for the log command's --date option.
By default, dates are shown in the original time zone (either committer's or author's).
If -local is appended to the format (e.g., iso-local), the user's local time zone is used instead.

option.name: --date-order
tip: Show no parents before all of its children are shown, but otherwise show commits in the commit timestamp order.

option.name: --decorate
tip: Print out references (branch and tag names) that point at the shown commits.

option.name: --dense
tip: Only the selected commits are shown, plus some to have a meaningful history.

option.name: --disk-usage
tip: Suppress normal output; instead, print the sum of the bytes used for on-disk storage by the selected commits or objects.
This is equivalent to piping the output into git cat-file --batch-check='%(objectsize:disk)', except that it runs much faster (especially with --use-bitmap-index).
See the CAVEATS section in git-cat-file(1) for the limitations of what "on-disk storage" means.
With the optional value human, on-disk storage size is shown in human-readable string(e.g. 12.24 Kib, 3.50 Mib).

option.name: --do-walk
tip: Overrides a previous --no-walk.

option.name: --encoding
tip: Commit objects record the character encoding used for the log message in their encoding header; this option can be used to tell the command to re-code the commit log message in the encoding preferred by the user.
For non plumbing commands this defaults to UTF-8.
Note that if an object claims to be encoded in X and we are outputting in X, we will output the object verbatim; this means that invalid sequences in the original commit may be copied to the output.
Likewise, if iconv(3) fails to convert the commit, we will quietly output the original object verbatim.

option.name: --exclude
tip: Do not include refs matching <glob-pattern> that the next --all, --branches, --tags, --remotes, or --glob would otherwise consider.
Repetitions of this option accumulate exclusion patterns up to the next --all, --branches, --tags, --remotes, or --glob option (other options or arguments do not clear accumulated patterns).

option.name: --exclude-first-parent-only
tip: When finding commits to exclude (with a ^), follow only the first parent commit upon seeing a merge commit.
This can be used to find the set of changes in a topic branch from the point where it diverged from the remote branch, given that arbitrary merges can be valid topic branch changes.

option.name: --exclude-hidden
tip: Do not include refs that would be hidden by git-fetch, git-receive-pack or git-upload-pack by consulting the appropriate fetch.hideRefs, receive.hideRefs or uploadpack.hideRefs configuration along with transfer.hideRefs (see git-config(1)).
This option affects the next pseudo-ref option --all or --glob and is cleared after processing them.

next.name: fetch
tip: Exclude fetch hidden refs.

next.name: receive
tip: Exclude receive hidden refs.

next.name: uploadpack
tip: Exclude uploadpack hidden refs.

option.name: --exclude-promisor-objects
tip: (For internal use only.) Prefilter object traversal at promisor boundary.
This is used with partial clone.
This is stronger than --missing=allow-promisor because it limits the traversal, rather than just silencing errors about missing objects.

option.name: --expand-tabs
tip: Perform a tab expansion (replace each tab with enough spaces to fill to the next display column that is a multiple of <n>) in the log message before showing it in the output. --expand-tabs is a short-hand for --expand-tabs=8, and --no-expand-tabs is a short-hand for --expand-tabs=0, which disables tab expansion.

option.name: --extended-regexp
tip: Consider the limiting patterns to be extended regular expressions instead of the default basic regular expressions.

option.name: --filter
tip: Only useful with one of the --objects*; omits objects (usually blobs) from the list of printed objects.
The <filter-spec> may be one of the following:

option.name: --filter-print-omitted
tip: Only useful with --filter=; prints a list of the objects omitted by the filter.
Object IDs are prefixed with a "~" character.

option.name: --filter-provided-objects
tip: Filter the list of explicitly provided objects, which would otherwise always be printed even if they did not match any of the filters.
Only useful with --filter=.

option.name: --first-parent
tip: When finding commits to include, follow only the first parent commit upon seeing a merge commit.

This option can give a better overview when viewing the evolution of a particular topic branch, because merges into a topic branch tend to be only about adjusting to updated upstream from time to time, and this option allows you to ignore the individual commits brought in to your history by such a merge.

option.name: --fixed-strings
tip: Consider the limiting patterns to be fixed strings (don't interpret pattern as a regular expression).

option.name: --format
tip: Pretty-print the contents of the commit logs in a given format, where <format> can be one of oneline, short, medium, full, fuller, reference, email, raw, format:<string> and tformat:<string>.
When <format> is none of the above, and has %<placeholder> in it, it acts as if --pretty=tformat:<format> were given.

option.name: --full-history
tip: Same as the default mode, but does not prune some history.

option.name: --glob
tip: Pretend as if all the refs matching shell glob <glob-pattern> are listed on the command line as <commit>.
Leading refs/, is automatically prepended if missing.
If pattern lacks ?, *, or [, /* at the end is implied.

option.name: --graph
tip: Draw a text-based graphical representation of the commit history on the left hand side of the output.
This may cause extra lines to be printed in between commits, in order for the graph history to be drawn properly.
Cannot be combined with --no-walk.

option.name: --graph-indent
tip: When used with --graph, indent visual roots (commits with no parents or whose parents are not shown) to differentiate them from commits that are vertically adjacent but unrelated.
Enabled by default.
Use --no-graph-indent to disable or set log.graphIndent to set a default preference.

option.name: --graph-lane-limit
tip: When --graph is used, limit the number of graph lanes to be shown.
Lanes over the limit are replaced with a truncation mark ~.
By default it is set to 0 (no limit), zero and negative values are ignored and treated as no limit.

option.name: --grep
tip: Limit the commits output to ones with a log message that matches the <pattern> regular expression.
With more than one --grep=<pattern>, commits whose message matches any of the <pattern> are chosen (but see --all-match).

option.name: --grep-reflog
tip: Limit the commits output to ones with reflog entries that match the <pattern> regular expression.
With more than one --grep-reflog, commits whose reflog message matches any of the given patterns are chosen.
It is an error to use this option unless --walk-reflogs is in use.

option.name: --header
tip: Print the contents of the commit in raw-format; each record is separated with a NUL character.

option.name: --ignore-missing
tip: Upon seeing an invalid object name in the input, pretend as if the bad input was not given.

option.name: --in-commit-order
tip: Print tree and blob ids in order of the commits.
The tree and blob ids are printed after they are first referenced by a commit.

option.name: --indexed-objects
tip: Pretend as if all trees and blobs used by the index are listed on the command line.
Note that you probably want to use --objects, too.

option.name: --invert-grep
tip: Limit the commits output to ones with a log message that do not match the <pattern> specified with --grep=<pattern>.

option.name: --left-only
tip: List only commits on the respective side of a symmetric difference, i.e. only those which would be marked < resp. > by --left-right.

option.name: --left-right
tip: Mark which side of a symmetric difference a commit is reachable from.
Commits from the left side are prefixed with < and those from the right with >.
If combined with --boundary, those commits are prefixed with -.

option.name: --max-age
tip: Limit the commits output to specified time range.

option.name: --max-count
tip: Limit the output to the first <number> commits that would be shown.

option.name: --max-count-oldest
tip: Limit the output to the last <number> commits that would be shown.

option.name: --max-parents
tip: Show only commits which have at least (or at most) that many parent commits.
In particular, --max-parents=1 is the same as --no-merges, --min-parents=2 is the same as --merges. --max-parents=0 gives all root commits and --min-parents=3 all octopus merges.

option.name: --maximal-only
tip: Restrict the output commits to be those that are not reachable from any other commits in the revision range.

option.name: --merge
tip: Show commits touching conflicted paths in the range HEAD...<other>, where <other> is the first existing pseudoref in MERGE_HEAD, CHERRY_PICK_HEAD, REVERT_HEAD or REBASE_HEAD.
Only works when the index has unmerged entries.
This option can be used to show relevant commits when resolving conflicts from a 3-way merge.

option.name: --merges
tip: Print only merge commits.
This is exactly the same as --min-parents=2.

option.name: --min-age
tip: Limit the commits output to specified time range.

option.name: --min-parents
tip: Show only commits which have at least (or at most) that many parent commits.
In particular, --max-parents=1 is the same as --no-merges, --min-parents=2 is the same as --merges. --max-parents=0 gives all root commits and --min-parents=3 all octopus merges.

option.name: --missing
tip: A debug option to help with future "partial clone" development.
This option specifies how missing objects are handled.

option.name: --missing-only
tip: When used together with --missing=print or --missing=print-info, suppress all output for present objects and print only the missing ones.
The selected --missing= format is preserved (so --missing=print-info still emits path= / type= fields), but the leading "?" prefix used by the non--z forms is omitted.
This is useful for scripting, as a simpler and faster alternative to post-processing the output of --missing=print.

option.name: --no-abbrev-commit
tip: Show the full 40-byte hexadecimal commit object name.
This negates --abbrev-commit, either explicit or implied by other options such as --oneline.
It also overrides the log.abbrevCommit variable.

option.name: --no-all
tip: Disable --all.

option.name: --no-all-match
tip: Disable --all-match.

option.name: --no-alternate-refs
tip: Disable --alternate-refs.

option.name: --no-author-date-order
tip: Disable --author-date-order.

option.name: --no-basic-regexp
tip: Disable --basic-regexp.

option.name: --no-bisect
tip: Disable --bisect.

option.name: --no-bisect-all
tip: Disable --bisect-all.

option.name: --no-bisect-vars
tip: Disable --bisect-vars.

option.name: --no-boundary
tip: Disable --boundary.

option.name: --no-cherry
tip: Disable --cherry.

option.name: --no-cherry-mark
tip: Disable --cherry-mark.

option.name: --no-cherry-pick
tip: Disable --cherry-pick.

option.name: --no-children
tip: Disable --children.

option.name: --no-commit-header
tip: Suppress the header line containing "commit" and the object ID printed before the specified format.
This has no effect on the built-in formats; only custom formats are affected.

option.name: --no-count
tip: Disable --count.

option.name: --no-date-order
tip: Disable --date-order.

option.name: --no-decorate
tip: Disable --decorate.

option.name: --no-dense
tip: Disable --dense.

option.name: --no-do-walk
tip: Disable --do-walk.

option.name: --no-exclude-first-parent-only
tip: Disable --exclude-first-parent-only.

option.name: --no-exclude-promisor-objects
tip: Disable --exclude-promisor-objects.

option.name: --no-expand-tabs
tip: Perform a tab expansion (replace each tab with enough spaces to fill to the next display column that is a multiple of <n>) in the log message before showing it in the output. --expand-tabs is a short-hand for --expand-tabs=8, and --no-expand-tabs is a short-hand for --expand-tabs=0, which disables tab expansion.

option.name: --no-extended-regexp
tip: Disable --extended-regexp.

option.name: --no-filter
tip: Turn off any previous --filter= argument.

option.name: --no-filter-print-omitted
tip: Disable --filter-print-omitted.

option.name: --no-filter-provided-objects
tip: Disable --filter-provided-objects.

option.name: --no-first-parent
tip: Disable --first-parent.

option.name: --no-fixed-strings
tip: Disable --fixed-strings.

option.name: --no-graph
tip: Disable --graph.

option.name: --no-graph-indent
tip: When used with --graph, indent visual roots (commits with no parents or whose parents are not shown) to differentiate them from commits that are vertically adjacent but unrelated.
Enabled by default.
Use --no-graph-indent to disable or set log.graphIndent to set a default preference.

option.name: --no-header
tip: Disable --header.

option.name: --no-ignore-missing
tip: Disable --ignore-missing.

option.name: --no-in-commit-order
tip: Disable --in-commit-order.

option.name: --no-indexed-objects
tip: Disable --indexed-objects.

option.name: --no-invert-grep
tip: Disable --invert-grep.

option.name: --no-left-only
tip: Disable --left-only.

option.name: --no-left-right
tip: Disable --left-right.

option.name: --no-max-parents
tip: Show only commits which have at least (or at most) that many parent commits.
In particular, --max-parents=1 is the same as --no-merges, --min-parents=2 is the same as --merges. --max-parents=0 gives all root commits and --min-parents=3 all octopus merges.

option.name: --no-maximal-only
tip: Disable --maximal-only.

option.name: --no-merge
tip: Disable --merge.

option.name: --no-merges
tip: Do not print commits with more than one parent.
This is exactly the same as --max-parents=1.

option.name: --no-min-parents
tip: Show only commits which have at least (or at most) that many parent commits.
In particular, --max-parents=1 is the same as --no-merges, --min-parents=2 is the same as --merges. --max-parents=0 gives all root commits and --min-parents=3 all octopus merges.

option.name: --no-missing-only
tip: Disable --missing-only.

option.name: --no-not
tip: Disable --not.

option.name: --no-object-names
tip: Only useful with --objects; does not print the names of the object IDs that are found.
This inverts --object-names.
This flag allows the output to be more easily parsed by commands such as git-cat-file(1).

option.name: --no-objects
tip: Disable --objects.

option.name: --no-objects-edge
tip: Disable --objects-edge.

option.name: --no-objects-edge-aggressive
tip: Disable --objects-edge-aggressive.

option.name: --no-oneline
tip: Disable --oneline.

option.name: --no-parents
tip: Disable --parents.

option.name: --no-perl-regexp
tip: Disable --perl-regexp.

option.name: --no-quiet
tip: Disable --quiet.

option.name: --no-reflog
tip: Disable --reflog.

option.name: --no-regexp-ignore-case
tip: Disable --regexp-ignore-case.

option.name: --no-relative-date
tip: Disable --relative-date.

option.name: --no-remove-empty
tip: Disable --remove-empty.

option.name: --no-reverse
tip: Disable --reverse.

option.name: --no-right-only
tip: Disable --right-only.

option.name: --no-show-pulls
tip: Disable --show-pulls.

option.name: --no-show-signature
tip: Disable --show-signature.

option.name: --no-simplify-by-decoration
tip: Disable --simplify-by-decoration.

option.name: --no-simplify-merges
tip: Disable --simplify-merges.

option.name: --no-single-worktree
tip: Disable --single-worktree.

option.name: --no-sparse
tip: Disable --sparse.

option.name: --no-stdin
tip: Disable --stdin.

option.name: --no-timestamp
tip: Disable --timestamp.

option.name: --no-topo-order
tip: Disable --topo-order.

option.name: --no-unpacked
tip: Disable --unpacked.

option.name: --no-use-bitmap-index
tip: Disable --use-bitmap-index.

option.name: --no-walk
tip: Only show the given commits, but do not traverse their ancestors.
This has no effect if a range is specified.
If the argument unsorted is given, the commits are shown in the order they were given on the command line.
Otherwise (if sorted or no argument was given), the commits are shown in reverse chronological order by commit time.

option.name: --no-walk-reflogs
tip: Disable --walk-reflogs.

option.name: --not
tip: Reverses the meaning of the ^ prefix (or lack thereof) for all following revision specifiers, up to the next --not.
When used on the command line before --stdin, the revisions passed through stdin will not be affected by it.
Conversely, when passed via standard input, the revisions passed on the command line will not be affected by it.

option.name: --object-names
tip: Only useful with --objects; print the names of the object IDs that are found.
This is the default behavior.
Note that the "name" of each object is ambiguous, and mostly intended as a hint for packing objects.

In particular: no distinction is made between the names of tags, trees, and blobs; path names may be modified to remove newlines; and if an object would appear multiple times with different names, only one name is shown.

option.name: --objects
tip: Print the object IDs of any object referenced by the listed commits. --objects foo ^bar thus means "send me all object IDs which I need to download if I have the commit object bar but not foo".
See also --object-names below.

option.name: --objects-edge
tip: Similar to --objects, but also print the IDs of excluded commits prefixed with a "-" character.
This is used by git-pack-objects(1) to build a "thin" pack, which records objects in deltified form based on objects contained in these excluded commits to reduce network traffic.

option.name: --objects-edge-aggressive
tip: Similar to --objects-edge, but it tries harder to find excluded commits at the cost of increased time.
This is used instead of --objects-edge to build "thin" packs for shallow repositories.

option.name: --oneline
tip: This is a shorthand for --pretty=oneline --abbrev-commit used together.

option.name: --parents
tip: Print also the parents of the commit (in the form "commit parent...:").
Also enables parent rewriting, see History Simplification above.

option.name: --perl-regexp
tip: Consider the limiting patterns to be Perl-compatible regular expressions.

option.name: --pretty
tip: Pretty-print the contents of the commit logs in a given format, where <format> can be one of oneline, short, medium, full, fuller, reference, email, raw, format:<string> and tformat:<string>.
When <format> is none of the above, and has %<placeholder> in it, it acts as if --pretty=tformat:<format> were given.

option.name: --progress
tip: Show progress reports on stderr as objects are considered.
The <header> text will be printed with each progress update.

option.name: --quiet
tip: Don't print anything to standard output.
This form is primarily meant to allow the caller to test the exit status to see if a range of objects is fully connected (or not).
It is faster than redirecting stdout to /dev/null as the output does not have to be formatted.

option.name: --reflog
tip: Pretend as if all objects mentioned by reflogs are listed on the command line as <commit>.

option.name: --regexp-ignore-case
tip: Match the regular expression limiting patterns without regard to letter case.

option.name: --relative-date
tip: Synonym for --date=relative.

option.name: --remotes
tip: Pretend as if all the refs in refs/remotes are listed on the command line as <commit>.
If <pattern> is given, limit remote-tracking branches to ones matching given shell glob.
If pattern lacks ?, *, or [, /* at the end is implied.

option.name: --remove-empty
tip: Stop when a given path disappears from the tree.

option.name: --reverse
tip: Output the commits chosen to be shown (see Commit Limiting section above) in reverse order.
Cannot be combined with --walk-reflogs.

option.name: --right-only
tip: List only commits on the respective side of a symmetric difference, i.e. only those which would be marked < resp. > by --left-right.

option.name: --show-linear-break
tip: When --graph is not used, all history branches are flattened which can make it hard to see that the two consecutive commits do not belong to a linear branch.
This option puts a barrier in between them in that case.
If <barrier> is specified, it is the string that will be shown instead of the default one.

option.name: --show-pulls
tip: Include all commits from the default mode, but also any merge commits that are not TREESAME to the first parent but are TREESAME to a later parent.
This mode is helpful for showing the merge commits that "first introduced" a change to a branch.

option.name: --show-signature
tip: Check the validity of a signed commit object by passing the signature to gpg --verify and show the output.

option.name: --simplify-by-decoration
tip: Commits that are referred by some branch or tag are selected.

option.name: --simplify-merges
tip: Additional option to --full-history to remove some needless merges from the resulting history, as there are no selected commits contributing to this merge.

option.name: --since
tip: Show commits more recent than <date>.
As a special case, today means the last midnight.

option.name: --since-as-filter
tip: Show all commits more recent than <date>.
This visits all commits in the range, rather than stopping at the first commit which is older than <date>.

option.name: --single-worktree
tip: By default, all working trees will be examined by the following options when there are more than one (see git-worktree(1)): --all, --reflog and --indexed-objects.
This option forces them to examine the current working tree only.

option.name: --skip
tip: Skip <number> commits before starting to show the commit output.

option.name: --sparse
tip: All commits in the simplified history are shown.

option.name: --stdin
tip: In addition to getting arguments from the command line, read them from standard input as well.
This accepts commits and pseudo-options like --all and --glob=.
When a -- separator is seen, the following input is treated as paths and used to limit the result.
Flags like --not which are read via standard input are only respected for arguments passed in the same way and will not influence any subsequent command line arguments.

option.name: --tags
tip: Pretend as if all the refs in refs/tags are listed on the command line as <commit>.
If <pattern> is given, limit tags to ones matching given shell glob.
If pattern lacks ?, *, or [, /* at the end is implied.

option.name: --timestamp
tip: Print the raw commit timestamp.

option.name: --topo-order
tip: Show no parents before all of its children are shown, and avoid showing commits on multiple lines of history intermixed.

option.name: --unpacked
tip: Only useful with --objects; print the object IDs that are not in packs.

option.name: --until
tip: Show commits older than <date>.

option.name: --use-bitmap-index
tip: Try to speed up the traversal using the pack bitmap index (if one is available).
Note that when traversing with --objects, trees and blobs will not have their associated path printed.

option.name: --walk-reflogs
tip: Instead of walking the commit ancestry chain, walk reflog entries from the most recent one to older ones.
When this option is used you cannot specify commits to exclude (that is, ^<commit>, <commit1>..<commit2>, and <commit1>...<commit2> notations cannot be used).

option.name: -z
tip: Instead of being newline-delimited, each outputted object and its accompanying metadata is delimited using NUL bytes.
Output is printed in the following form:

next.name: rev-parse
tip: Pick out and massage parameters and messages from Git.

option.name: --abbrev-ref
tip: A non-ambiguous short name of the objects name.
The option core.warnAmbiguousRefs is used to select the strict abbreviation mode.

option.name: --absolute-git-dir
tip: Like --git-dir, but its output is always the canonicalized absolute path.

option.name: --after
tip: Parse the date string, and output the corresponding --max-age= parameter for git rev-list.

option.name: --all
tip: Show all refs found in refs/.

option.name: --before
tip: Parse the date string, and output the corresponding --min-age= parameter for git rev-list.

option.name: --branches
tip: Show all branches, tags, or remote-tracking branches, respectively (i.e., refs found in refs/heads, refs/tags, or refs/remotes, respectively).

option.name: --default
tip: If there is no parameter given by the user, use <arg> instead.

option.name: --disambiguate
tip: Show every object whose name begins with the given prefix.
The <prefix> must be at least 4 hexadecimal digits long to avoid listing each and every object in the repository by mistake.

option.name: --exclude
tip: Do not include refs matching <glob-pattern> that the next --all, --branches, --tags, --remotes, or --glob would otherwise consider.
Repetitions of this option accumulate exclusion patterns up to the next --all, --branches, --tags, --remotes, or --glob option (other options or arguments do not clear accumulated patterns).

option.name: --exclude-hidden
tip: Do not include refs that would be hidden by git-fetch, git-receive-pack or git-upload-pack by consulting the appropriate fetch.hideRefs, receive.hideRefs or uploadpack.hideRefs configuration along with transfer.hideRefs (see git-config(1)).
This option affects the next pseudo-ref option --all or --glob and is cleared after processing them.

option.name: --flags
tip: Do not output non-flag parameters.

option.name: --git-common-dir
tip: Show $GIT_COMMON_DIR if defined, else $GIT_DIR.

option.name: --git-dir
tip: Show $GIT_DIR if defined.
Otherwise show the path to the .git directory.
The path shown, when relative, is relative to the current working directory.

option.name: --git-path
tip: Resolve "$GIT_DIR/<path>" and takes other path relocation variables such as $GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, $GIT_INDEX_FILE...: into account.
For example, if $GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY is set to /foo/bar then "git rev-parse --git-path objects/abc" returns /foo/bar/abc.

option.name: --glob
tip: Show all refs matching the shell glob pattern pattern.
If the pattern does not start with refs/, this is automatically prepended.
If the pattern does not contain a globbing character (?, *, or [), it is turned into a prefix match by appending /*.

option.name: --is-bare-repository
tip: When the repository is bare print "true", otherwise "false".

option.name: --is-inside-git-dir
tip: When the current working directory is below the repository directory print "true", otherwise "false".

option.name: --is-inside-work-tree
tip: When the current working directory is inside the work tree of the repository print "true", otherwise "false".

option.name: --is-shallow-repository
tip: When the repository is shallow print "true", otherwise "false".

option.name: --keep-dashdash
tip: Only meaningful in --parseopt mode.
Tells the option parser to echo out the first -- met instead of skipping it.

option.name: --local-env-vars
